camps.name: AUNTY NE CHASHMA LAGAYA.
camps.idea: WORLD: wedding nights under plum-and-marigold shamiana bokeh. Each frame shows the piece worn at true size: an ear from behind, a hand on the red-velvet arm of a gilt banquet chair, a collarbone, or a wrist. From the frame edge, an aunty's hand (rani-pink pallu, no rings or bangles) holds gold half-moon reading glasses between the camera and the piece. Inside the lens the piece is an honest crop of the same photograph at about 2x; outside the lens it stays true size. One frame therefore carries both the macro proof and the real scale. GRAPHIC SYSTEM: Velista headline in bone on the bokeh. Three gold-light hairline leaders (1.5 px, ending in 10 px open circles) run from points inside the lens to 'FIG.' callouts, each a Jost caps fact label over her Hinglish verdict in Cormorant italic quotes: the fact goes in the label, her opinion in the quote. A hairline scale tag reads 'IN HER LENS ABOUT 2× · ACTUAL 25 MM'. A round AUNTY APPROVED seal (Jost set on a circle around a small reading-glasses glyph) sits top right, and the F2 card sits on plum. WORDS: the inspection is the pain ('PICHLI SHAADI MEIN BHI YAHI THA?'). Her verdict is the proof. 'Then she asked for the link' is the outcome, the 'Where is this from?' hook that is our best CTR ever. AUNTY BHI LEGI. and AUNTY KI KITTY BHI LEGI. close BUY3 and BUY4. RULES: the lenses never reflect eyes or a face. The glass never tints the metal. White shell pearls are graded neutral on plum. Footer for all ten camps: CASH ON DELIVERY only, never free shipping (hard rule 5). MOTION (cards 1 and 5): the glasses drift in, the lens racks from blur to sharp, the callouts draw on one by one, and the seal turns 30 degrees and settles.
camps.why: Every wedding guest has survived the aunty inspection, so her reading glasses turn the buyer's biggest fear ('will it look cheap at a wedding?') into honest proof: true size outside the lens, craft at about 2x inside it. 'Then she asked for the link' echoes our best-ever hook. It is the jury's top camp (7.92) and is as bold as it is sellable, so it leads.
camps.graft: story-4 FULL HOUSE gives card 10 its kitty-party BUY4 close: AUNTY KI KITTY BHI LEGI, four pieces at 30% off with BUY4. culture-1 SUITABLE MATCH gives the Duo Link card its best line: LOVE CUM ARRANGED.

camps.name: SHAADI KA VIDEO.
camps.idea: WORLD: paused frames from a 1996 wedding cassette. Each slow piece is generated clean and pin-sharp from its listing reference: an ear from behind under a red-and-saffron shamiana with a tuberose gajra, a hand on a lavender lehenga's zari border, warm tungsten fairy-light bokeh. Each piece then gets the 90s video effect it really is, laid over it in HTML and masked off the metal: four-point star twinkles on the bokeh only (the Quatrefoil is the biggest, sharpest star in the frame), a feathered heart vignette around the aqua heart, a butterfly-shaped wipe whose body lands on the Papillon ring, soft-focus glow on everything except the brushed satin, a sunburst flare on the bokeh behind the Baguette disc, a black-and-white flashback in which only the gold tone keeps its colour, an iris closing on the Verdant Cushion, a crash-zoom onto the toggle clasp. GRAPHIC SYSTEM: a Jost on-screen display in one corner ('PLAY ▶ 12 · 12 · 1996', 'PAUSE ‖', 'REW ◀◀'). One tracking-noise band crosses the background only. The effect is named as a 90s title card in Velista (gold-light fill, thin bone outline, soft cocoa drop shadow), with a Cormorant italic subtitle saying what it is now. The Naira wordmark is the videographer's studio bug, top right. The F2 card is a cocoa lower third. GRAFT: the BUY3/BUY4 end cards stack four VHS spines with handwritten HTML labels (MEHENDI · HALDI · SANGEET · RECEPTION) and the line 'TAPE 4 OF 4 · COLLECT ALL FOUR'. RULES: no generated text, timestamps, camera logos, real studio watermarks or couples' names. Effects never sit on the stones. Pre-order pieces carry no claims and no water. Only ears from behind, hands and napes appear, never faces. MOTION (cards 1 and 3): the tape rolls in with a tracking band and colour bleed, the effect plays as an overlay, then a PAUSE freeze lands on the pin-sharp piece. Optional sound: tape hiss and a shehnai sting.
camps.why: It is the craziest idea every 35-54 buyer gets in a blink: the slow pre-order pieces really are the cassette's effects (star filter, heart frame, butterfly wipe, iris), so a joke the family forwards also shows the exact product. All the kitsch lives in masked overlays on a verified plate, and the four-tape BUY4 end card makes the offer the punchline.
camps.graft: art-3 FOUR SHOWS DAILY: the four wedding functions become four tapes. The end cards are four handwritten VHS spines: COLLECT ALL FOUR = BUY4 at 30% off, any three = BUY3 at 20% off.

camps.name: BEST OF THREE.
camps.idea: WORLD: angoothi dhoondhna after the pheras. A polished brass paraat of milky water with a few blush petals. Only hands and forearms appear: mehendi, red kalava thread, never chooda, bangles or other rings. A hand bursts out of the milk holding the piece rigid between its fingertips, inside a flash-frozen crown of droplets, shot either side-on against an oxblood shamiana or top-down, where the paraat is a perfect brass circle with one sharp sparkle. Only waterproof-tagged pieces go into the milk, so the picture proves waterproof with no claims panel. GRAPHIC SYSTEM: a hand-chalked match scoreboard in Jost, top left ('BRIDE 2 · GROOM 1 · ROUND 3', with hairline tally strokes), that plays out across the carousel as one match. The round's result is the Velista headline. A hairline locator runs to a Jost size label. GRAFT: a cartographer's two-row scale bar ('PARAAT · ABOUT 45 CM' over a long bar, 'RING · 17 MM INSIDE' over a stub), so the splash never cheats on size. A small chip, 'milk, haldi, the whole shaadi: waterproof', appears on tagged pieces only. The F2 card sits on cocoa. WORDS: ROUND ONE: HERS. leads to BEST OF THREE. and then CLEAN SWEEP. The 'HER 3 · HIM 0' score lives in the Jost scoreboard, never in Velista, which has no digits. A men 18-24 card reads LET HER WIN. BUILD: the splash and hand are a Higgsfield plate, and the verified piece is composited in as a rigid cut-out so its construction never changes. MOTION (card 1): the hand bursts up, the milk crown rises and falls, petals arc, and the scoreboard ticks over with a chalk stroke.
camps.why: It is the one Indian ritual whose climax is finding jewellery, and its own rule, best of three, is BUY3. A hand bursting out of milk proves waterproof without a claim, and the paraat scale bar keeps every ring honest about size.
camps.graft: surreal-1 COW FOR SCALE: the honest two-row scale bar (PARAAT · ABOUT 45 CM / RING · 17 MM INSIDE) keeps a dramatic splash true to size.

camps.name: MUJHE KUCH NAHI CHAHIYE.
camps.idea: WORLD: an Indian home at night under one tungsten bulb. A mother's cupped hands (about 60, haldi on one fingertip, a faded cotton pallu, no bangles or rings) receive the piece. A daughter's hands close a chain at her nape. A first-salary son's hand (pale office-shirt cuff) holds out earrings across a laminate table. A 38-year-old's own wrist rinses a tiffin at a 7 am steel sink. GRAFT: the rooms carry factory plastic on the sofa arm and the good crockery behind showcase glass as soft set dressing, so the picture says she saves every good thing for later. GRAPHIC SYSTEM: the Hindi sentence huge in Velista bone across the dark top third, with an oversized gold-light Cormorant open quote hanging into the margin, signed 'MUMMY, EVERY YEAR' in Jost. THE YEAR LADDER runs down the left edge: 32 lines of '1994   MUJHE KUCH NAHI CHAHIYE' through 2025 in Jost 17 px caps, fading from 15% to 55% like a till roll. The last line breaks the pattern in terracotta: '2026', then the piece's name in Cormorant italic, then 'Order anyway.' The F2 card sits on cocoa. WORDS: her refusal is the pain, the gift is the outcome, and 'Nobody knows her ring size' is the objection. 'AB TUM BHI KEHTI HO' turns the sentence on the buyer herself for the BUY3 close: hers, Mausi's, yours. RULES: water appears only on the Triple Coil, which is tagged waterproof. Hands, napes and wrists only. One piece per picture. MOTION (card 1): the ladder ticks in year by year with a soft calendar tick, the headline drops in whole, one light sweep crosses the metal, and the 2026 line types itself.
camps.why: It is the truest sentence in Indian family life, set as a 32-year ladder that ends in 'Order anyway.'. It sells three pieces without discount talk (Mummy, Mausi, you) and reaches both buyers: the daughter or first-salary son, and the 38-year-old who now says it herself. The jury put it second overall, with an 8.71 for sell.
camps.graft: story-5 PLASTIC MAT UTAARNA: the sofa plastic and guest crockery become set dressing (she saves everything good), and its permission line, 'made for Tuesdays', goes on the shell-pearl card.

camps.name: PARCHHAI.
camps.idea: WORLD: low December sun (21 Dec, the longest shadows of the year) on hot lime-washed walls in palette colours: terracotta, sky, saffron, coral-deep, pista. The real piece hangs from one brass nail or rests on a plaster ledge at true size and keeps its own true contact shadow. Its long cast shadow on the wall is not its shape but its meaning: the two stones throw two people holding hands, the butterfly ring throws a butterfly in flight, the toggle throws a pinky promise, the braided hoops throw a circle of sangeet dancers, the Duo Link throws two hands tying a knot, the bold dome throws the moon, the Verdant Eternity's vine climbs into a family tree. Each meaning-shadow is generated in the plate as a hard cast gobo silhouette. It is never pasted on, never redraws the piece, and is always a pure silhouette with no faces. GRAPHIC SYSTEM: every headline is set twice. The object line is in Velista. Directly beneath it falls its own cast type-shadow, skewed 22 degrees and soft-edged in cocoa at 55% multiply, reading the meaning line in Cormorant italic, at the same sun angle and length as the photograph. A Jost sundial tick sits at the frame edge ('4:52 PM · 21 DEC'), and a size line sits at the root of the piece ('RING 17 MM INSIDE · SHADOW NOT INCLUDED'). The F2 card sits in the sunlit band; gold-light is reserved for the lit side of the metal. GRAFT: on the BUY3 cards one sentence runs through three shadows across the carousel and only finishes on the last one ('A SENTENCE IN THREE PIECES'). RULES: walls and sun only, never water. One jewel in the light. MOTION (cards 1 and 5): a sun time-lapse drags the light lower and the shadow stretches from the piece's true outline into its meaning while the type-shadow lengthens in sync. On card 5 the dancers' shadow whirls to a dhol beat while the hoops never move.
camps.why: It is the best type idea in the batch: the headline casts its own shadow under the same sun as the photo, and the shadow says what the gift means. Every slow piece becomes a message for one named person on her December list. 'SHADOW NOT INCLUDED' owns the scale with a smile.
camps.graft: type-5 LAMBI PARCHHAI: one sentence threaded through three shadows across the carousel on the BUY3 cards (A SENTENCE IN THREE PIECES), so the three-piece order reads as one line.

camps.name: UDHAAR KHATA.
camps.idea: WORLD: night, a hard on-camera flash with a crisp black drop shadow. The borrower's hand is caught mid-grab (chipped plum nail polish, a black hair tie on the wrist, no jewellery), with motion blur on the fingertips only, at a walnut dressing table, a wardrobe-mirror corner angled to a blank wall, a wedding suitcase potli, or a half-open bedroom door. Didi keeps the account in a red cloth bahi-khata. GRAPHIC SYSTEM: the borrower's famous excuse is the Velista headline, in bone on flash-black, with an oversized terracotta Cormorant open quote. A torn ledger strip crosses the lower third: bone paper, faint blue rules, a double red margin, and an oxblood cloth spine with SVG stitch marks. Its Jost column heads read TAREEKH · KISNE LIYA · KYA · WAPAS?, and three Cormorant italic entries pass the same piece down the family, so the WAPAS column fills with ?, ?? and ???. A terracotta KHATA BAND rubber stamp (distressed SVG ink, rotated -8 degrees) overlaps the offer box. The F2 card closes the frame. Borrowers are family roles only, never real names. WORDS: the excuses are the pain (SIRF EK FUNCTION KE LIYE., KAL WAPAS KAR DUNGI.). The piece being wanted is the outcome. 'It fits anyone' is the objection. 'Buy three, get yours back' is the offer. RULES: the ledger in the picture, if one appears, is blank; every word is HTML. No water. The borrower's hand wears nothing else. MOTION (card 1): a two-frame flash pop with a shutter sound, then the ledger rows write themselves in, each ? pops into the WAPAS column, and the stamp thuds down with a 3 px shake.
camps.why: Every sister has a borrower. The flash-caught grab reads as a small crime at 200 px, and a ledger filling with question marks is a type joke people screenshot. 'Buy three, get yours back' is the most natural three-piece logic on the table.

camps.name: BIJLI GAYI.
camps.idea: WORLD: an Indian room at night, the second the power cuts. Rooms rotate: a limewashed drawing room, a mehendi-night bedroom with a brass thaali, an old Kolkata stairwell, a bridal dressing room with no mirror, a terrace with dead fairy lights. The room goes black; one candle off-frame catches the piece, and each finish throws its own kind of light across the walls as soft round dots, never star glints: the toggle's warm scatter, the Prism's lilac, pink and lemon confetti, green fireflies from the Verdant cushion, one icy blue spot from the aqua heart, one beam up the stairwell from the single pavé link, the brushed satin's low glow, four soft moons from the Petite Square's pearls. The piece is the brightest and most saturated thing in the frame, the grammar our winning ads share. GRAPHIC SYSTEM: 'BIJLI GAYI.' in Velista bone, lit by the piece: a radial mask brightens the letters nearest the jewel and lets the rest fall into the dark. The second beat is in the piece's own sampled colour ('TOGGLE ON.' in gold-light, 'HARA NAHI GAYA.' in green, 'NEELA NAHI GAYA.' in icy blue). A two-row SVG rocker switchboard in Jost reads 'BIJLI · OFF' (switch down, grey) and 'CHAMAK · ON' (switch up, lit). A size line appears wherever a frame is magnified, and the F2 card is bone on ink. GRAFT: the closing card's double meaning, 'BIJLI AAYI.': the lights come back, and the bijli who walked in is her. The BUY3 card is BACKUP, the inverter pack. RULES: no water, no mirrors or faces, no branded inverter, no glow that blurs claws or pavé. Prism light stays lilac, pink, lemon and white. MOTION (card 1): the fan winds down, a thunk, a family's 'ohhh' off-screen, the light blooms across the walls; at 5 s the inverter beeps the lights back on and the piece is still the brightest thing in the room.
camps.why: Every Indian knows the moment the power goes, and making the piece the room's only light is a real product demonstration: polish, pavé and satin each make their own light, inside our proven one-bright-piece-on-black frame. The BIJLI AAYI double meaning ends the carousel on her.
camps.graft: type-2 DO MATLAB: its two-meanings device closes the camp. 'BIJLI AAYI.' means both 'the power is back' and 'the stunner walked in'.

camps.name: EK MATRA KI KAMI.
camps.idea: WORLD: blank wedding invitations, one per function (roka, mehendi, sangeet, ring ceremony, haldi, shaadi, reception): thick ivory or dyed deckled card with abstract foil borders and nothing printed, shot top-down in warm window light on that function's silk (oxblood, sage-deep, plum, cocoa) with a marigold or a dholak rim at the edge. The real piece lies exactly where one stroke of a Devanagari word is missing: a chain laid dead straight is the shirorekha of पक्का; two green studs are the chandrabindus of मेहँदी? हाँ; the Prism arcs are the bindus of रंग-बिरंगी; a ring is the dot of अंगूठी; a bracelet is the bar of रौनक; a choker's collar and drop are the bar and the ा of हार (necklace, and also 'defeat'); a stone hanging under a snake chain is the ू of बूँद; hoops are the ी of शादी and हल्दी; a bangle is the anusvara of कंगन. GRAPHIC SYSTEM: the Devanagari word in SVG foil (Rozha One for display, Tiro Devanagari for small text; a gold-light gradient with a 1 px emboss, matched to the card's perspective) with one matra left out. The jewel sits in its place inside a 1.5 px dashed gold-light circle with a Jost micro-label ('मात्रा · 16.8 MM'). A Velista transliteration headline sits above the card, the Naira wordmark is the invitation's foil seal, and the F2 card sits below. The offer line reads 'TEEN FUNCTION, TEEN MATRA · BUY3 · 20% OFF'. GRAFT: under every word, a Roman bilingual dictionary gloss (a Jost phonetic, then Cormorant 'sense 1: the word, sense 2: the piece'), so non-Hindi readers get the joke and Hindi readers get it twice. RULES: the generated card carries no monograms, deity marks or pseudo-letters; every glyph is HTML. A 'SHOWN ABOUT 2X' tag appears wherever a piece is drawn larger than true scale. MOTION (card 1): the foil word writes itself in sign-writer stroke order, stops at the gap for 0.6 s, then the dashed ring tightens onto the real clasp and one foil glint sweeps across the word and the jewel.
camps.why: It is the only idea where the jewel literally becomes a letter: a necklace completes the word for necklace and a bangle completes the word for bangle. That makes type and picture one, an award-level move no Indian brand has made. The grafted Roman gloss lets non-Hindi readers in, and every invitation is a function she attends this month.
camps.graft: type-2 DO MATLAB: a two-script dictionary gloss under each Devanagari word (phonetic, sense 1 the word, sense 2 the piece), which fixes the jury's 'only Hindi readers get it' risk without making the idea tamer.

camps.name: AAJ KA BHAAV.
camps.idea: WORLD: a vintage jeweller's glass counter at night under one hard spot and a tube-light reflection. It holds maroon velvet trays, ring rolls, a faceless velvet bust, an antique oxidised hand balance with its right pan empty, and (graft) a jeweller's digital pan scale. Above hangs the red dot-matrix LED rate board every Indian jewellery shop has; on Naira's board the rate never moves. GRAPHIC SYSTEM: an SVG LED panel in a brushed-aluminium frame, with Jost glyphs under a 5 px round-dot mask (lit dots saffron fading to coral-deep with a soft glow, unlit dots oxblood at 15%). It reads 'AAJ KA BHAAV ₹999 / PIECE' over 'KAL KA BHAAV ₹999', and a third row below a chrome rule reads 'THOK BHAAV · BUY3 · 20% OFF'. The scale's readout, also HTML, shows the listed grams only where the listing states them (Toggle 12 g, Serpentine 10 g, Tubogas 2.7 g, Mint Pear 2.7 g) under the line 'BY THE PIECE, NOT BY THE GRAM'. The Naira wordmark is the shop's fascia in gold-light. The Velista headline sits over the velvet with a Cormorant italic beat, and the F2 card sits on a velvet plinth. RULES: never name a metal rate, never a struck or compare-at price. 'Kal bhi yahi' needs the owner to hold prices for the whole flight. Grade neutral so maroon never tints rhodium or stones; no pearls on maroon. Trays, busts and glass carry no shop names, hallmarks or tags. MOTION (card 1): the tube light ticks on, the LED scrolls like a marquee, flickers through a 'rate change' and lands on exactly the same number, and the THOK BHAAV line scrolls in.
camps.why: In a wedding season of record metal rates, a jeweller's LED board whose rate never moves ('Kal bhi yahi') answers her loudest money worry, and THOK BHAAV turns BUY3 into the wholesale rate she already understands. The grafted scale shows real listed grams, so the honesty is the joke.
camps.graft: surreal-4 HALKA PHULKA: its honest listed-weight numeral moves onto a jeweller's digital scale beside a rate board that never changes (BY THE PIECE, NOT BY THE GRAM), turning a weight claim into proof.

camps.name: PAINTED BIGGEST.
camps.idea: WORLD: the real piece, with its real shadow, lies on a commissioned and credited gouache miniature on wasli paper in which palaces, elephants and gardens are fingernail-sized, so the jewel is the biggest thing in the picture. That is hieratic scale, the old painters' rule. Scenes: a Mewar lake palace at night, a dry Rajput desert road to a palace gate, a Kishangarh lakeside pavilion, a Mughal charbagh, a Rajasthani roofscape of chhatris at golden hour, a fort's two rings of walls, a caravan under a star, the pachisi court. RULES: no human figures, no inscriptions (cartouches painted blank). Lakes appear only under waterproof pieces (Halo Curve, Verdant Circlet); every other scene is dry. GRAPHIC SYSTEM: every ad is a royal album page: an oxblood rule, a gold-light floral scroll border, a marbled margin. The Velista headline sits in the top cartouche. Then the fixed kicker in Cormorant italic, 'Old painters drew the most important thing biggest.', followed by the honest size in Jost ('REAL SIZE: 17 MM') with a hairline scale bar in the margin. The F2 card sits in the lower cartouche, with a small credit line for the painter. The BUY3 cards become an album spread of three windows (ear, neck, wrist) with the line 'Make yourself the biggest thing in the picture.' GRAFT: a living miniature painter is commissioned and credited, never AI miniatures, and the painted world moves in parallax as the heir to the dhol-tasha bracelet the owner loved. A riderless baraat of caparisoned elephants carrying naqqara kettle-drums walks up the chain to the sailor ring, the drums beating with no players. MOTION (card 2): procession parallax, drums beating, lamps flickering; the piece never moves.
camps.why: Hieratic scale is a real art-history rule that makes the real piece the biggest thing in the picture without enlarging it, and 'Old painters drew the most important thing biggest' tells her she is the important one. A credited living painter and a moving baraat whose drums beat by themselves give the owner the dhol-tasha motion she asked for, in a world we have never shot.
camps.graft: art-4 THE WALL DANCES: a commissioned, credited real artist instead of AI pastiche, and a painted world that moves (a riderless baraat with naqqara drums beating as it walks up the chain), the owner's dhol-tasha wish told through a new art form.

camps.name: AUNTY NE CHASHMA LAGAYA.
camps.idea: WORLD: one Indian wedding seen the way an aunty sees it, one inspection at a time, in clock order: the sangeet at 10:40 PM, the catering tent's chai counter at 1 a.m., the rooftop mehendi under an indigo sky, the reception baithak by diya light, the aunty's own turn at the sangeet, the pheras at 2 a.m., the reception at midnight, the cocktail lounge, the haldi the morning after (the one daylight frame) and the kitty party the Sunday after. Each card has its own light and place, so the carousel never repeats a world; plum carries the night and every card. DEVICE: every frame shows the real piece worn at true size (an ear from behind, a hand, a collarbone, a wrist) and, between the camera and the piece, an aunty's reading glasses: tortoiseshell half-moons held by an older hand whose wrist disappears into a rani-pink pallu. Inside the lens the finished ad shows an honest 2x crop of the same photograph, built in HTML from a 4K plate and clipped to the real rim; outside the lens the piece stays true size, and the type owns the magnification ('IN HER LENS ABOUT 2× · ACTUAL 25 MM'). On Reels the device becomes physical: her voice opens the ad ('Beta, zara idhar aana'), the headline stays out of focus until her glasses lock on (THE SQUINT), and the lens is live. Her face is never seen: her hand, her pallu and her Hinglish verdicts are enough. ARC: cards 1-4 she inspects (the plait, two unmatched stones, two hidden stars, eight mismatched pearls, and the buyer talks back); card 5 turns the joke: she wears the toggle herself and writes her BUY3 order slip, striking out the padosan ('agli baar'); cards 6-9 she checks with both lenses at the pheras (GOLD TONE weds SILVER TONE), counts twenty baguettes twice, matches colours on a tailor's matching card, and keeps a repeat register at the haldi; card 10 pays off the cliffhanger: four aunties, four ring sizes, one adjustable ring, and the padosan back in ('is baar main bhi'), BUY4.
camps.insight: At an Indian wedding, the review that decides whether jewellery looks expensive is given from 20 cm by an aunty in reading glasses, and every woman has survived it. Our buyer's real fear ('will it look cheap up close?') is the fear of that lens, so we hand her the lens and let the piece pass. Reading glasses arrive in the early forties: our core buyer (women 35-44, then 45-54) is both the inspected and, more and more, the inspector, so the camp flatters both sides, and card 5 makes the aunty the customer. Wedding season adds the second fear the camp sells against: five functions and an aunty who remembers repeats. That turns BUY3 from a discount into a need (a new piece for each function) and turns slow stock into the point, because a piece this wedding hasn't seen yet is exactly what she wants now. The device also fixes our oldest craft problem: a 16 mm stud is invisible at true size in a feed, and an honest 2x lens makes it big without lying about its size.
camps.textualGraphic: THE INSPECTION REPORT, a type system invented for this idea, built in HTML over the photograph with kit.css tokens and fonts. (0) INSPECTION LOG: one line above the headline in Jost 300 15 px, tracking .24em, gold-light at 70% (ink on the haldi card), x 128, Feed y 84, Story y 276, giving place, time and count ('SANGEET · 10:40 PM · INSPECTION 1 OF 10'). The ten logs run in clock order through one wedding, from the sangeet at 10:40 PM to the kitty party on Sunday at 4 PM, so the carousel has a plot and every single ad hints at nine more. (1) EYE-CHART HEADLINE: Velista caps, bone #F4F0E8, flush left at x 128 from Feed y 112, in two or three rows that shrink like an optician's chart, each row about 0.75 of the one above (three rows: 124/92/68 px), line-height .98, tracking .02em. In the x 72 gutter each row carries its acuity mark in Jost 300 16 px gold-light at 70%: 6/60, 6/36, 6/24. The headline gets harder to read as it goes, so the eye leans in, as she does. (1b) THE SQUINT, motion only: on every Reel the eye chart opens at blur 10 px and 98% scale and snaps sharp, with the click of the frame, on the frame where her glasses lock on; the viewer needs her glasses to read the ad. Statics are always sharp. (2) BEAT: Cormorant Garamond italic 500, 34-44 px, gold-light, at most two lines, set under the lens in the calm dark band (Feed y 806-930), so the eye reads headline, lens, beat, card; on card 4 the Feed carries only the punch, under the headline. (3) THE LENS: the tortoiseshell rim is in the photograph. The glass is filled in HTML with the same photograph at exactly 2.0x about the lens centre (background-size twice the canvas, background-position at minus the lens centre), with a clip-path traced to the rim's inner edge, an inset shadow 0 0 24px rgba(26,22,20,.35) and one 3 px bone arc at 35% on the upper left as the glass highlight. No tint, no sharpening, no retouch inside the lens. Plates are generated at 4K (2160 x 3840) so the 2x crop uses native pixels, and the earrings and the ring are shot in an 11 cm field, so the lens shows them at about 19.6 Feed px per mm, over the ads-500 line of 19 px per mm for 'magnified'. THE LIVE LENS, motion only: a second copy of the same clip, scaled 2.0 about the lens centre and clipped to the rim, used only on frames where the rim is still, so a pearl's swing plays at 2x inside the glass and at true size outside it. (4) THE REPORT: up to three gold-light 1.5 px hairline leaders, each starting at a 10 px open circle on METAL inside the lens (never on a stone), with one 90-degree elbow, ending at a callout in a side gutter (x 72-300 or x 740-1008). Each callout is a Jost 500 caps 20 px label, tracking .16em, bone, carrying the fact from the product card ('FIG. 1 · OPEN PLAIT, SEE-THROUGH CORE'), over Cormorant italic 34 px gold-light in curly quotes carrying her Hinglish verdict ('itna barik kaam?'). Facts live in the label, opinion lives in the quote, and a quote never carries a claim. (5) SCALE TAG: a 1.5 px gold-light hairline box hugging the rim with a 24 px tick, in Jost 500 caps 17 px .14em bone: 'IN HER LENS ABOUT 2× · ACTUAL 25 MM ACROSS'. The type owns the magnification and always prints the listed size plainly. (6) THE SEAL: a 150 px roundel top right (Feed x 858, y 84), a gold-light 1.5 px double ring with Jost 500 caps 15 px .28em on a circular path, 'AUNTY APPROVED ✦ AUNTY APPROVED ✦', and an SVG half-moon glasses glyph (two flat-topped D shapes and a bridge, 2 px stroke) at its centre, rotated -12 degrees. It is oxblood on the haldi card; card 10 reads KITTY APPROVED; on Reels it turns 30 degrees and settles. (7) THE 6/6 LINE: the last and smallest row of the eye chart, at Feed y 948: a 120 px terracotta #B5502F hairline (the red line on a real chart), '6/6' in Jost 300, then claims and materials in Jost 500 caps 18 px .2em bone at 85%, only what the product card allows. The line you need glasses to read is the proof she checked. (8) THE F2 CARD on a plum scrim (transparent at Feed y 880, #4A2540 at 92% from y 990): the Naira wordmark in bone at 56 px, NAME in Jost 500 caps 26 px .2em, price in Cormorant 56 px (Noto ₹ subset), one line in Jost 26 px, the offer box in Jost 500 caps 26 px with the kit's rotated-square gold-light separator, and the footer CASH ON DELIVERY in Jost 20 px. CARD DEVICES, each grown out of the lens: an analogy bar, CHAI : GLASS :: TIGER EYE : CRYSTAL (Halo Curve); a star-atlas constellation around the two little stars (Verdant Circlet); a same-scale LINE-UP of the eight pearls traced from the photo, 'FIND THE ODD ONE OUT. all eight.', plus a balance-beam glyph for 27.6 G (Baroque); her ORDER SLIP with '4 · padosan ke liye' scribbled out and 'agli baar' beside it (Toggle); a wedding-card 'weds' in Cormorant italic, a gathbandhan knot glyph and a two-name key (Duo Link); a mala of twenty numerals, counted twice (Baguette); a tailor's MATCHING CARD with a staple, three pinked swatches colour-picked from the stones and a fourth reading 'YOUR BLOUSE · ANY NEUTRAL' (Prism); AUNTY'S REPEAT REGISTER, stamped 'first sighting' (Marquise); four sized tags on a US 5 to 9 KITTY RULER (Verdant Eternity). GRID: every plate is 9:16, with the piece and lens between 33% and 53% of its height, calm bokeh from 14% to 32% and soft darkness below 55%. Feed crops the plate from 12% to 82% of its height: log y 84, headline y 112-390, lens zone y 404-790 with callouts and column devices in the side gutters, beat or band device y 806-930, 6/6 line y 948, card y 990-1266. Story uses the full plate (text only between y 270 and 1250): log y 276, headline from y 304 at the Feed sizes, beat about y 520-640, lens zone y 650-1010, and a compact card y 1030-1250 with the 6/6 line folded in. Text stays under about 30% of the frame.
camps.brandFeatures: The Naira wordmark lives only in the F2 card (bone on plum, 56 px), like a jeweller's name on a receipt, never on the picture. The F2 card is unchanged: name, price, one line, offer box, footer CASH ON DELIVERY, so every ad still reads as Naira at the foot. Type stays inside the kit: Velista for the eye-chart headline (caps, no digits or ₹); Cormorant Garamond italic for beats, verdicts, prices and the wedding-card 'weds'; Jost for the inspection log, FIG labels, acuity marks, scale tag, seal, analogy bar, line-up, order-slip numerals, matching card, register, kitty ruler and the 6/6 line. Palette tokens carry the night: plum as the card, bone headlines, gold-light for every hairline, terracotta for the eye chart's red line, cocoa for the Prism ground, ink and oxblood on the haldi card. The lens-and-FIG report is a direct cousin of the founder-approved FIG layout on the live lotus Story (the graphic quality bar), so the camp extends a look the owner already ships. Owned assets recur on every ad: the half-moon glasses glyph in the seal, the INSPECTION n OF 10 log, the eye chart and the 6/6 line, plus, on Reels, the same aunty voice and THE SQUINT. Ten ads read as one series in the feed.
camps.palette: Plum #4A2540 stays the card ground on every ad and the night on cards 1, 5 and 7. The other worlds change key so the carousel never repeats one: amber bulb and brushed steel (2), deep indigo rooftop sky (3), diya points on plum velvet (4), a marigold-and-mango-leaf mandap haze with the fire only as orange bokeh in one corner (6), a cocoa #3B2620 lounge (8), haldi daylight in marigold and saffron #E8A33A (9), plum velvet with cream lace (10). Amber, indigo and fire live in the photograph only, never in type. Marigold bokeh is kept soft and pulled toward saffron, so the piece is always the most saturated thing in frame. Rani pink appears only in the aunty's pallu (photograph only, never in type); on card 10 four pallus (rani pink, mustard, parrot green, peacock blue) show only as slivers at the frame edges. Glasses are dark tortoiseshell. Type: bone #F4F0E8 headlines; gold-light #E4C889 hairlines, seal, verdicts and the 'weds'; terracotta #B5502F for the 6/6 red line; ink #1A1614 and oxblood #6E1F23 on the haldi card. Grade: white shell pearls and clear stones neutral, rhodium cool, 18k gold tone warm-neutral and never brassy. Amber, diya and fire light stay in fills and bokeh, never the key on the metal, and the glass never tints the metal.
camps.sellLever: Trust turned into basket size. The inspection is the TRUST layer (does it look cheap up close? the 2x lens says no, with the true size printed beside it). Wedding season supplies the reason to buy three now: five functions and an aunty who remembers repeats, so BUY3 means one new piece per function, not a discount; card 9, the carousel and the order slip all say so. Every card carries BUY 2 · 10% OFF ◆ BUY 3 · 20% OFF in the card, and every primary text has 'Any three, 20% off with BUY3' ending before character 125. Card 5 makes BUY3 her order slip (mere liye, bahu ke liye, samdhan ke liye) on the ₹999 stock anchor and strikes out a fourth line; card 10 pays it off as BUY4, the kitty: four aunties, four ring sizes, one ring that opens from US 5 to 9. Slow stock becomes the point, because 'first sighting' is honest for pieces this wedding hasn't seen. Ad-set map for the ₹5,000-a-day CBO: PAIN = cards 1, 9; OUTCOME = 3, 7, 8; OBJECTION = 2, 4, 6; OFFER = 5, 10. Layers: EDUCATION 2, 6, 8; TRUST 1, 3, 4, 7, 9; SELL 5, 10 (retarget with 5 and 10 plus the TRUST cards). The four Reels (1, 5, 7, 10) lead prospecting, because the voice and the squint hook in the first second. The statics also run as one ten-card carousel in clock order with card 10 last, because this account converts best when she can see several pieces and choose. Cards 1-5 run first, 6-10 second.
camps.carouselText: Every wedding has an aunty who leans in. We handed her the glasses: one wedding night, ten pieces, ten inspections. Aunty remembers repeats, so: any three, 20% off with BUY3; any four, 30% off with BUY4. About 2× in her lens, true size outside. Cash on delivery.
camps.changes:
PUSHED (k01 v2, 20 Nov):
1) The hook is now sound and focus as well as picture. Every Reel opens on the aunty's voice ('Beta, zara idhar aana', a voice actor, no real person imitated) and on THE SQUINT: the eye-chart headline stays out of focus until her glasses lock on, so the viewer needs her glasses to read the ad.
2) No edit passes (ads-500 RULINGS §3). Cards 1 and 5 are Kling clips made from the approved still and played reversed (a playback reversal, no pixel edit), so the glasses arrive and land on the verified frame. Card 7 runs forward from the still with THE LIVE LENS (the same clip at 2.0x, clipped to the still rim), so the pearl's swing plays at 2x. Card 10 is post-only, because five hands are too risky to move. That makes four Reels instead of two.
3) INSPECTION LOG: a Jost time stamp and 'INSPECTION n OF 10' on every ad turn the carousel into one wedding in clock order, from the sangeet at 10:40 PM to the kitty party on Sunday.
4) Fewer plum worlds, so no two cards share a light: an amber-bulb chai counter (2), an indigo rooftop mehendi (3), a diya-lit baithak (4), the pheras mandap with the fire only as bokeh (6), a cocoa cocktail lounge with a bar cart (8), haldi daylight (9) and plum velvet with lace (10). Plum stays the card ground.
5) Truer, bigger scale: the earrings and the ring are now shot in an 11 cm field, so the lens shows them at about 19.6 Feed px per mm (over the 19 px per mm line for 'magnified'). The bracelet is shot at 13 cm, the toggle and the choker at 15 cm.
6) Sharper words. Card 3: 'AUNTY KO TAARE DIKH GAYE.' (the Hindi idiom for being dazzled, made literal by two hidden stars). Card 6: 'GOLD TONE weds SILVER TONE.', set like a shaadi card at the pheras, with the sixteen knot connectors as sixteen gathbandhans. Card 7: 'SHE COUNTED TWENTY. TWICE.' Card 8: 'ITNE RANG, EK KAAN PE?' Card 4: the buyer talks back, 'Isiliye toh liya.' Card 1's beat names the distance: 'From 20 cm she checked every wire.'
7) Crazier proofs:
- an analogy bar, CHAI : GLASS :: TIGER EYE : CRYSTAL (2);
- a same-scale, police-style line-up of the eight traced pearls, 'FIND THE ODD ONE OUT. all eight.', and a balance-beam glyph for 27.6 G (4);
- the order slip's fourth line, 'padosan ke liye', scribbled out with 'agli baar' (5), paid off on card 10 with 'is baar main bhi';
- a gathbandhan knot glyph and a two-name key (6);
- a mala count, done twice (7);
- a tailor's matching card with a staple and a fourth swatch, 'YOUR BLOUSE · ANY NEUTRAL', that teaches the styling tip (8);
- AUNTY'S REPEAT REGISTER (9);
- four aunties with four ring sizes on a US 5 to 9 kitty ruler (10).
8) Offer logic: BUY3 is framed as the cure for repeats (three functions, three pieces) in the carousel, on card 9 and in the slip; BUY4 is the kitty.
9) Copy fixes:
- No quote carries a claim: card 2's 'meri ungli mein bhi aayegi' became 'toh main bhi pehen loon?', and card 10's BUAJI asks 'mujhe bhi aayegi?'.
- Woven FIG. 2, 'NO STONES', became 'MIRROR POLISH ON EVERY WIRE' (the hoops' copy notes avoid stone words).
- Every primary text was reworked to 152-170 characters, with 'Any three, 20% off with BUY3' ending by character 124 (it did not before on cards 1, 2, 7, 8 and 9).
- The Baroque 6/6 line now carries 27.6 G.
- Claims were re-checked per card: Toggle and Baroque have no waterproof claim and no water imagery; Baguette and Prism have no claims at all.
10) Risk cut on card 10: only the fingertips and thumbs of the aunties enter, at the frame edges, with slivers of four pallus.
KEPT: the name, the eye chart, the honest 2x lens, the FIG report, the seal, the 6/6 line, the F2 card, the card 5 twist, the chai rhyme, the haldi card and every product lock.
FLAGS for the producer:
(a) concept-50/RULINGS.md §6 asks for 'FREE INSURED SHIPPING · CASH ON DELIVERY' on every ad, but this brief's hard rule 5 bans free shipping, and on 20 Nov the store still charged ₹150 below ₹3,000. The footer stays CASH ON DELIVERY, with a slot reserved for the shipping line if the owner confirms the checkout matches.
(b) Marquise Drop Choker gold has 15 units, under the ads-500 rule of 20+, but it is on the slow-stock list. Show gold only and confirm stock at render.
(c) Baroque (18) and Duo Link (17) are also under 20 and on the slow-stock list; no scarcity counts are printed.
(d) The aunty's voice is a voice actor's own performance, never a celebrity sound-alike.
truth: card 3 (Verdant Circlet) constellation. The 12 px SVG sparks were drawn exactly over the two metal stars inside the 2x lens, which would have hidden the real stars behind drawn ones (rule 1, and the lens's own no-retouch rule). They now sit just outside the circlet, each with a 1 px tick pointing to its real star, and the open-circle nodes leave the metal and stones inside them visible. The textual graphic's 'constellation over the two little stars' now reads 'around'.
truth: I checked all ten ads against rules 1-8 and found no other breaks. Each prompt carries its card's lock with the must-stay clause, names reference 1 as the authority, and uses the card's own reference 2. Every variant shown is in stock (Marquise gold has 15). Each picture holds one product, shows no faces, eyes or eyebrows, and forbids generated text. Claims follow each card: there is no water on Toggle or Baroque, and Baguette and Prism make no claims. Prices are live and the codes real (BUY2/3/4). There is no free shipping and no compare-at or struck price. Velista headlines carry no digits or ₹. Each lens prints its 2x with the real size. No brand, person or interface is imitated. The aunty, her seal and her quotes are a dramatised character, never presented as a customer review, rating or name. All primary texts run 152-170 characters with BUY3 ending by character 124.

ads.title: The inspection
ads.variant: Default Title, 18k gold tone (the only variant). One hoop worn; the pair is on the card line.
ads.picture: The sangeet at 10:40 PM under the shamiana: plum dark, marigold fairy-light bokeh. We stand just behind a young woman: right ear, black hair in a low bun, bare nape, an ivory raw-silk blouse collar. The Woven Gold Hoop hangs from her lobe at true size, in an 11 cm field, close enough that the braid reads even outside the glass. From the left edge the aunty's hand, wrist lost in a rani-pink pallu, holds tortoiseshell half-moon reading glasses so the left lens sits between us and the lower half of the hoop. In the finished ad that lens holds an honest 2x crop of the same photograph: the open plait, its see-through core and every wire's own highlight, at about 20 px per mm. On the Reel the ad opens on her voice, 'Beta, zara idhar aana', and the headline stays out of focus until her glasses lock on. At 200 px: a half-moon lens full of bright gold braid, held by a hand everyone recognises.
ads.prompt: Vertical 9:16 editorial wedding-night photograph at 4K (2160 x 3840), 100 mm macro-portrait lens at ear height, seen from just behind and slightly to the left of a young Indian woman at a sangeet under a shamiana. Reference 1 is the authority on this exact piece: copy the earring's construction exactly and ignore its block and light; reference 2 is a detail of the braid. FIDELITY: one hoop on her right earlobe: a round hoop 25 mm across, a 5-6 mm open plait of polished round wires laid in pairs and braided in chevrons over a see-through core of finer wires; one flat mirror-polished 8 mm disc at the top on the latch side; one thin hinged latch wire; no stones; no bottom loop; 18k gold tone, mirror polish. It must stay a many-wire open braid, never a smooth tube, a simple twist or an oval; do not redesign or add anything. SCALE: worn, the hoop hangs from the lobe at about half the ear's height, a little smaller than a 27 mm coin; field of view about 11 cm wide, so the hoop is about 23% of the frame's width and the whole ear fits in frame; a soft contact shadow where it touches the neck. BODY: her head is turned well away; the right frame edge falls just behind the jaw hinge, so no cheek, eyebrow, eye, nose or lips appear anywhere; black hair in a low bun, bare nape with fine downy hair, an ivory raw-silk blouse collar low in frame. THE AUNTY: from the left edge, an older Indian woman's hand, about sixty, warm brown skin with soft creases, short bare nails, no rings, bangles, watch or mehendi, the wrist under a rani-pink silk pallu, holds half-moon reading glasses with thin dark tortoiseshell frames by one temple arm so the left lens hovers about 8 cm in front of the hoop, centred on its lower half, the lens about 40% of the frame's width; the glass is perfectly clear, showing what is behind it at the same size, undistorted and untinted, reflecting nothing, never a face or eyes. WORLD: a plum-dark shamiana at night, soft marigold fairy-light bokeh. COMPOSITION: hoop and lens between 33% and 53% of the frame height; from 14% to 32% calm out-of-focus plum bokeh with soft marigold points and nothing else; below 55% soft ivory silk and plum shadow, darker toward the bottom. LIGHT: soft warm fill from the fairy lights above left; one small hard specular kicker from behind right puts a crisp highlight on every polished wire of the braid and on the disc. Warm-neutral 18k gold tone, never brassy or orange. NEGATIVES: no text, letters, numbers or logos anywhere; no face or eyes anywhere, never reflected in the lens; one product only: no second earring, necklace or nose pin; no rings or bangles on anyone; no star-shaped glints.

ads.motion: Kling 3.0, 5 s, start frame = the approved still (no edit pass, no end frame). Kling animates the departure: over 5 s the aunty's hand slowly lowers the glasses and withdraws them out of the left edge; the fairy-light bokeh twinkles and drifts right; one loose hair at the nape lifts once; the camera is locked. The head, ear and hoop never move: no swing, no turn, no morph. EDIT: the clip plays reversed at 1.6x (a playback reversal, no pixel edit). From 0 to 3.1 s the glasses glide in from the left and lock over the hoop, landing exactly on the verified frame, which holds from 3.1 to 5.6 s. POST: from frame one THE SQUINT keeps the eye chart at blur 10 px; it snaps sharp on the lock frame (3.1 s). From 3.1 to 3.7 s the 2x lens composite racks from an 8 px blur to sharp; from 3.7 to 4.9 s the three leaders draw on, 0.4 s each with a soft tick, each verdict fading up after its line; at 5.1 s the seal turns 30° and settles with a small overshoot. The card is on screen from frame one. Sound: at 0.2 s a voice actor (a warm woman of about sixty speaking Hinglish, imitating no one) says 'Beta, zara idhar aana.'; the glasses click at the lock; a long 'hmmm' runs under the leaders; at the seal she says '...link bhejna.', over shehnai and a party murmur.
ads.risk: The braid inside the lens: the model may smooth the plait into a rope, which the 2x lens exposes. The tighter 11 cm field invites the known 1.4x scale drift: verify the hoop at 21-25% of the frame width. Rings or bangles may creep onto the aunty's hand. In the Kling clip, reject any frame where the hoop swings or is redrawn. Hedge take: the lens moved off the hoop onto the nape, with the magnified view built as a separate circular inset cropped from the hoop and labelled the same way.
ads.why10: It names the fear every wedding guest has (will it look cheap up close?) in the first second, in sound ('Beta, zara idhar aana') and in focus (the blurred headline), then answers it in the same frame: a true 25 mm outside the lens, the plait at about 20 px per mm inside. The hand and the half-moon glasses read as 'aunty' before a word is read, 'Then she asked for the link' borrows our best-ever hook, and the 11 cm field finally makes a 25 mm hoop big at 200 px.

ads.title: Cutting chai
ads.variant: Default Title, 18k gold tone (the only variant).
ads.picture: 1:05 a.m. at the catering tent's chai counter, the hour when the real reviews happen: one bare amber bulb, a brushed steel counter, a dented brass kettle far behind. A young woman's hand curls round a small ribbed cutting-chai glass of milky brown tea. The Halo Curve Ring is on her index finger: the opaque banded tiger eye and the faceted pale champagne crystal set diagonally, corners nearly touching. From the top right the aunty's hand holds her half-moon glasses over the two stones. The prop is the proof (brown tea in clear glass, a brown stone beside a clear one), and the type turns it into an analogy: CHAI : GLASS :: TIGER EYE : CRYSTAL. Inside the lens both stones appear at 2x, bands beside facets; outside it, a ring that spans one finger.
ads.prompt: Vertical 9:16 editorial late-night photograph at 4K (2160 x 3840), 100 mm macro lens, a close view from slightly above of a young Indian woman's right hand at a wedding's catering-tent chai counter at 1 a.m. Reference 1 is the authority on this exact piece: copy the ring's construction exactly and ignore its cube, background and light; reference 2 shows it worn at true scale. FIDELITY: the ring on her index finger, stones on top: one smooth round 1.5 mm wire in 18k gold tone whose two ends pass side by side; each end holds one cushion stone in one slim plain polished bezel, set diagonally across the finger, corners nearly touching: one opaque banded golden-brown tiger eye about 11.8 mm with a softly faceted top, and one transparent faceted pale champagne crystal of about the same face. No small stones, no prongs, high polish. The tiger eye must stay opaque, banded and golden-brown, never transparent, glassy or a twin of the crystal; do not redesign or add anything. SCALE: the two stones together span about the width of the finger; field of view about 11 cm wide, so the ring is about 17% of the frame's width; her fingers curl round a small ribbed cutting-chai glass 7 cm tall, half full of milky brown tea, the glass about three and a half times the ring's width; a crisp contact shadow under the band. HAND: warm wheatish skin, natural texture, five fingers, correct anatomy, short bare nails, no other ring, no bangle, no watch. THE AUNTY: from the top right edge, an older Indian woman's hand, about sixty, warm brown skin with soft creases, short bare nails, no rings, bangles, watch or mehendi, the wrist under a rani-pink silk pallu, holds half-moon reading glasses with thin dark tortoiseshell frames so one lens hovers about 8 cm above the two stones, centred on them, about 38% of the frame's width; the glass is perfectly clear, showing what is behind it at the same size, undistorted and untinted, reflecting nothing, never a face or eyes. WORLD: a brushed steel counter top, one bare amber bulb out of frame above, a dented brass kettle blurred far behind, dark plum-brown night beyond. COMPOSITION: ring and lens between 33% and 53% of the frame height; from 14% to 32% calm dark bokeh with two or three soft amber points; below 55% soft, dark steel. LIGHT: soft warm amber fill from the bare bulb above left, kept off the metal's key; one small hard neutral specular kicker from behind right gives each bezel a bright edge, the tiger eye a silky band of light and the crystal one white catchlight; the 18k gold tone stays warm-neutral, never orange. NEGATIVES: no text, letters, numbers or logos anywhere; no faces, eyes or reflections of faces; one product only, no other jewellery on anyone; no steam over the ring; no spilled tea.

ads.title: Taare dikh gaye
ads.variant: Default Title, 18k gold tone (the only variant). One stud worn.
ads.picture: The rooftop mehendi at 11:30 p.m.: a deep indigo night sky, strings of tiny warm fairy lights hanging out of focus like constellations. From behind and slightly above: hair up in a high bun, the edge of a bottle-green Banarasi blouse, and the Verdant Circlet Stud on the lobe, its deep green cushion stone sitting on top of the hollow, lopsided circlet. The aunty's hand comes down from the top edge and lowers her glasses over the ear. At 2x she finds what the rooftop missed: two little four-point stars on the circlet. The overlay joins stars and stones with a hairline constellation, and the headline turns the Hindi idiom for being dazzled into a literal fact: she saw stars.
ads.prompt: Vertical 9:16 editorial wedding-night photograph at 4K (2160 x 3840), 100 mm macro-portrait lens, seen from behind and slightly above a young Indian woman at a rooftop mehendi. Reference 1 is the authority on this exact piece: copy the earring's construction exactly and ignore its cube, background and light; reference 2 shows the mirrored pair from above. ads.motion: Kling 3.0, 5 s, start frame = the approved still, played forward. What moves: the round drop pearl sways about 8° on its loop and settles by 3.5 s; the fairy-light bokeh drifts slowly left; one petal of the gajra stirs once; the camera is locked. What never moves: the head, the ear, the disc and its twenty baguettes, and the aunty's hand and glasses (the rim must stay still so the lens composite stays registered). Cut at the last frame where the disc is unchanged. POST: THE LIVE LENS, a second copy of the same clip scaled 2.0 about the lens centre and clipped to the rim, so the swing plays at 2x inside the glass and at true size outside; from 0 to 0.6 s THE SQUINT headline sharpens; from 0.8 to 2.8 s the numerals 1 to 20 tick on round the disc, 0.1 s apart, each with a soft mala-bead click; from 3.0 to 3.6 s a second, fast pass runs 1 to 20 (TWICE) and the 20 is ringed; at 3.9 s the callouts draw on; at 4.5 s the seal turns 30° and settles. Sound: bead clicks over a soft shehnai, and the aunty's voice under the second pass: '...bees. Haan, bees.' Fallback if any frame redraws the disc: no Kling, the still with the post layers only.
ads.risk: The count: the listing macro shows exactly twenty baguettes (counted on 03.jpg), but the model may draw 16 or 24, and the numeral ring would expose it. Any take that is not exactly twenty is rejected, not retouched. 'Halo' is kept out of the prompt so there is no round centre stone. In motion, Kling may redraw the disc while the pearl swings: cut at the last clean frame or use the post-only fallback. Hedge headline if the count cannot be verified at 2x: 'SHE COUNTED THEM. TWICE.' with the numerals dropped.
ads.why10: Counting is the most aunty thing an aunty does, and 'twice' makes her a character. The mala count turns an abstract word (sunburst) into a number she can check herself, the swinging pearl is the product's own hook, and the live lens shows the swing at 2x without a single drawn pixel. The outcome line, 'she asked where you got them', is the 'kahan se liya?' every buyer wants.

camps.name: SHAADI KA VIDEO.
camps.idea: THE WORLD: the Indian shaadi video, in two tenses. PLAYBACK is the December 1996 cassette in every almirah, where the videographer threw every effect in his edit deck at the jewellery: the star filter, the heart frame, the butterfly wipe, the soft focus, the flashback, the page peel, the fast forward, the lens flare, the crash zoom, the iris that closes on THE END. REC is her own tape, being shot this season. Our ten slow pieces turn out to BE those effects, made solid: the Quatrefoil Éclat is the four-point star, the Aqua Heart hangs where the heart frame went, the Lilac Papillon is the butterfly the wipe was cut in, the Baguette Halo's disc is a flare with twenty rays, the Verdant Cushion is the last spark before the iris closes, the Toggle is where the crash zoom always landed. THE OSD IS THE ANGLE AND THE TENSE: REC (a terracotta dot, '2026 · YOUR TAPE') for OUTCOME, because in 1996 the effects were for the bride and this season they are hers. Playback covers everything the old tape knows: REW to the pain, FF past it, PAUSE and SLOW to check a doubt, STOP and EJECT for the offer (date stamp '12 · 12 · 1996'). TWO KINDS OF PLATE: IN THE TAPE (worn: ears from behind, a hand on a lehenga, a dance turn, the collarbones; cards 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 8, 10) and ON THE SHELF (the piece among the tape's own objects: a black VHS cassette under a 1996 video light, a gift from the 1996 gift table, velvet under the edit deck's lamp; cards 4, 7, 9). THE BUYER IS ON THE TAPE: the worn plates show women from their late thirties to their late forties in four skin tones, with a few silver strands in one twist and a hand in its forties. She is the didi, the mausi and the mother, and no Indian jewellery ad shows her. Every plate is generated clean, modern and pin-sharp from the listing photo as reference 1. All of 1996 is HTML laid on top and masked off the metal and stones. THE EFFECT IS THE HEADLINE, AND THE HEADLINE DOES THE EFFECT: the star filter's full stop is a star, the wipe crosses BUTTERFLY mid-transition, SOFT is blurred and FOCUS is sharp, FLASHBACK has its ghost, PEEL lifts off the page, FORWARD tears, the fake flare lands on the type and never on the piece, ZOOM rushes at you. THE FACTS LIVE WHERE THE TAPE WOULD WRITE THEM: the cassette label, the heart frame's edge, the VCR info screen and tape index, the 1996 gift register, the end credits, the four spines. RULES: no generated text, timestamps, camera logos, real studio marks or couples' names; effects never touch a stone or the metal; pre-order pieces carry no claims, no water and no dispatch promise; only ears from behind, napes, hands and collarbones; the Naira wordmark is the videographer's studio bug.
camps.insight: Every Indian family owns that cassette, and every buyer aged 35-54 has laughed at it in the family WhatsApp group: the star filter on every bangle, the bride floating in a heart, butterflies wiping from the pheras to the buffet. The kitsch was love: the videographer was trying to make the jewellery sparkle more than a 1996 camera could. Three truths make it sell. First, our slow pieces literally are those shapes (a four-point star, a heart, a butterfly, a sunburst), so the joke is the product description, and the forward ('this is literally mummy's video') carries the piece. Second, in 2026 she is not the bride. She is the didi, the mausi or the mother at five functions, and in 1996 only the bride got the heart frame. The REC cards give her the effects on her own tape, worn by a woman her age. Third, the tape is evidence. It recorded the pains she still has: the same jhumkas in all five tapes, casserole number seven in the gift register, the plated bangles that shone in the video and went dark in the almirah. So every playback card names a pain the whole family has watched, and every offer follows the tape's own logic: collect the effects, one piece per tape.
camps.textualGraphic: A VHS tape, paused or recording, built only from the kit. CANVAS: Feed 1080x1350 cut from the central 4:5 window of a 9:16 plate (nothing scaled); Story 1080x1920 native, text only between y270 and 1250. THE OSD (every card): top-left, Feed x72 y84 / Story y270. The transport word is Jost 500 30px tracked .14em, bone #F4F0E8 with a hard 2px 2px 0 ink shadow at 60% (the blocky VCR look). Its glyph is inline SVG (REC dot, triangle, double triangle, double bar, square, eject), never a font glyph. TWO TENSES: REC cards (1, 2, 3) carry a 22px terracotta #B5502F dot before 'REC' and the stamp '2026 · YOUR TAPE' (Jost 400 26px). Playback cards carry '12 · 12 · 1996', plus a card word where useful (FLASHBACK, GIFT TABLE). THE TITLE CARD: the effect's name in Velista caps 80-128px, letter-spacing .04em, ligatures off, fill gold-light #E4C889, a 1.5px bone outline and a soft cocoa drop shadow 0 6px 18px rgba(59,38,32,.7), like a 90s title super (set left or right on two lines wherever an ear would sit under it). EVERY TITLE PERFORMS ITS EFFECT and stays readable at 200px: (1) the full stop of FILTER is a 34px SVG four-point star; (3) the wipe's wing edge crosses THE BUTTERFLY, so the letter tops outside the wing are outline only; (4) THE SOFT carries a 2.5px blur and a bone bloom while FOCUS is pin-sharp; (6) FLASHBACK has a 1px bone ghost echo 8px left at 40%; (7) PEEL lifts, its letters turning 0 to -8 degrees with a cocoa underside; (8) the FF tear shears the lower half of FORWARD 14px right with a 3px RGB split; (9) a fake anamorphic streak crosses LENS FLARE and never the piece; (10) ZOOM is set 20% larger than THE CRASH with radial ghost streaks behind it. The subtitle (beat) is Cormorant Garamond italic 500, 40-52px, bone, never more than two lines. Gold-light is the colour of 18k gold tone, so in the black-and-white flashback the title and the gold tone are the only colours left. THE TRACKING BAND (playback only): one horizontal band 60-80px tall per playing tape (SVG feTurbulence noise, 3px RGB split, bone at 35% soft-light), across the background only, clipped by an alpha cut-out of the piece, hair and skin. (1) TWO TENSES. The three OUTCOME cards now record instead of play: a terracotta REC dot and '2026 · YOUR TAPE'. (3) THE BUYER IS ON SCREEN: the worn plates show women from their late thirties to their late forties (silver strands in card 2's twist, a hand in its forties on card 3, faint neck lines on card 10) in four skin tones. The core buyer is 35-54 and is never shown.

ads.prompt: Editorial on-model sangeet-night photograph, vertical 9:16 frame, photographed from behind the left shoulder in the middle of a dance turn: the back of the head with dark hair pulled up into a sleek high bun, the nape and the left ear, the head turned well away from the camera; the ear sits in the right third of the frame and the right edge of the frame falls just in front of the ear at the jaw hinge, so no cheek, cheekbone, temple, eyebrow, eyelash, eye, nose, lips or mouth appears anywhere, not even at the edge; the skin of an Indian woman in her late thirties with golden-olive medium skin, natural texture with visible pores and fine downy hair at the nape; the edge of a plum blouse embroidered with small round shisha mirrors at the shoulder. One hoop hangs from the lobe and has swung slightly out from the neck with the turn, its whole shape clear, frozen pin-sharp as if by a flash. Reference 1 is the authority on this exact piece; reference 2 shows its true size on the ear. The piece: an open C hoop 35 mm across with 1 straight post at its top end: 1 row of 15 slightly oval clear cubic zirconia, about 5 mm, facing out, each held by 4 claws in its own rounded cup with a fine beaded rim; the cups touch edge to edge, giving a scalloped outline; plain polished inner side; rhodium silver tone, high polish. It must stay separate oval stones in beaded cups, never a smooth line of round stones, never a small hoop, never a closed circle, never stones on the inner side. Do not redesign, restyle or resize it. SCALE: 35 mm across, about 1.3 times a 10-rupee coin; worn, it drops about 3.5 cm from the lobe, roughly two thirds of the ear's height; the frame is about 10 cm wide at the ear. WORLD: behind, a deep plum wall scattered with small soft round white dots of light from a turning mirror ball; the camera panned with the turn, so only the background dots are drawn into short soft curved streaks, while the ear, the hoop, the hair, the skin and the blouse are frozen completely sharp. LIGHT: one large soft cool-neutral fill from the right; one small hard specular kicker from the left makes every oval stone throw one crisp pure-white catchlight. COMPOSITION: the hoop sits just above the middle of the frame, from about 34 to 52 percent of the way down; the top third is calm plum wall for a title; the lower part is calm shoulder and blouse in soft shadow for a caption band. The photograph is clean, modern and pin-sharp on the subject: no VHS look, no scan lines, no star-shaped glints, no lens flare, no glow, no motion blur on the hoop or the ear; effects are added later. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermarks, no timestamps. No face, no eyes, no eyebrows. Only this one hoop; no other jewellery, no gajra.

camps.name: BEST OF THREE.
camps.idea: WORLD: angoothi dhoondhna after the pheras, broadcast live like a world final. A polished brass paraat about 45 cm across, milky water, a few blush and ivory petals, an oxblood shamiana with warm fairy lights (plum for the one rhodium chain). Only hands and forearms: hers with fresh mehendi and a red kalava thread, his with an ivory sherwani cuff and a kalava; never chooda, bangles or other rings. Only waterproof-tagged pieces go into the milk, so every plate proves waterproof without a claims panel. TEN BROADCAST MOMENTS, never the same splash twice: Match (cards 1-5) the burst, the wire cam, the photo finish, the decision (a victory fist), the trophy lift under a petal shower; Rematch (cards 6-10) the replay, day five's search, the sore loser's time-out ('best of four?'), the fix (he lets her win), the prize-giving (she runs the house). Cameras and light change with the moment: flash freeze, top-down daylight, a single lamp, low backlit hero, flash with falling petals, plum macro, a milk-line horizon, low diya-side light, raking tungsten, amber rim. WORDS: each Velista headline is the commentator's call, and every call is literally true of the piece: TOO CLOSE TO CALL (the ring's two ends), NOTHING TO LOSE (no stones), BEST OF THREE (three clear pears, then mint), DAY FIVE (a Test match's last day and the wedding's), BEST OF FOUR? (BUY4), MATCH FIXED (a thrown game and a settled rishta). The score lives in Jost because Velista has no digits. GRAPHIC SYSTEM: a hand-made match-day kit (live dot and score strip with chalk tallies, the call, one proof device born from the plate, the F2 card on cocoa), never a real channel's graphics. BUILD: the hands, milk and splash are a Higgsfield plate; the verified piece is composited as a rigid cut-out from its listing reference wherever the model drifts, so construction never changes. MOTION: cards 1, 3, 5, 6 and 10 animate in Kling 3.0 (the burst, the reach, the petal shower, the falling drop, the raised arm); type moves in HTML.
camps.insight: Every season our buyer stands at the edge of the same paraat: the one wedding ritual whose whole climax is finding a piece of jewellery (angoothi dhoondhna; eki beki in Gujarati homes). Two hands, a paraat of milk, one ring, the family screaming, and a rule everyone already knows: best of three, and whoever wins runs the house. The rule is our offer (BUY3), the milk is our proof (waterproof shown, not claimed), and India already watches this game the way it watches cricket, with a commentator in every family. The game is about finding a small thing nobody could see, which is exactly what these slow-stock pieces need: to be found, this wedding season, before the next function.
camps.textualGraphic: THE MATCH-DAY KIT, hand-made, never a real channel's, league's or app's graphics; at most four text elements per card, set with the restraint of the live lotus Story (tracked Jost labels, Cormorant italic asides, one huge Velista call). (1) SCORE STRIP, top-left x 72, y 84 (Story y 270): a 10 px terracotta #B5502F live dot (pulsing at 1 Hz in HTML), then Jost 500 caps 26 px, tracking .16em, bone #F4F0E8 on dark plates, ink #1A1614 on milk, at most 40 characters, e.g. 'ROUND 1 · HER 1 · HIM 0'. Her tallies are SVG chalk strokes, 2 px x 34 px, 9 px apart, saffron #E8A33A, edges roughened with feTurbulence and feDisplacementMap; HIM's slot is an empty 18 px hairline ring. The strip advances card by card, so the carousel reads as one match and a rematch while each card still reads alone, and the gags live inside it (WIRE CAM, UNDER REVIEW, DECISION, STONES LOST 0, DAY 5, TIME-OUT, HIM 1 struck out to 0, HOUSE: HERS). (2) THE CALL: Velista caps 100-120 px Feed, 116-136 px Story, line-height .98, tracking .02em, ligatures off, the winning words in saffron on dark or coral-deep #C8664A on milk; never digits, ₹, middle dots or dashes; a Cormorant Garamond italic 500 second beat at 44-48 px in gold-light #E4C889 or coral-deep, deadpan and lower-case. (3) ONE PROOF DEVICE born from the plate, different on every card and always carrying a listing fact in mm or a tag-backed claim: SIZE GUN (1: a speed-gun arc of five segments, US 5 to US 9, all lit, 'READS: ALL FIVE'), RIPPLE TEXT (2: SVG circles traced on the plate's own ripples, Jost on textPath), PHOTO FINISH (3: one 1 px saffron finish line through the gap between two fingertips, plus a bracket over the ring's two ends), TWO-ROW SCALE BAR (4: the COW FOR SCALE graft, 'PARAAT · ABOUT 45 CM' over 450 px and the band over a 6 px stub at the same 1 px per mm), ROUNDS TO PRIZE (5: leaders from three clear pears to ROUND 1-3 and from the mint pear to the offer), TWO DROPS (6: a replay freeze frame, milk falls off, cubic zirconia stays), SEARCH RETICLE (7: crosshair and range rings, a 10 mm target in a 45 cm paraat), THE BILL (8: a chalk-ruled receipt doing the BUY3 to BUY4 maths with '+ ₹189' in the margin), TOI ET MOI TAGS (9: his end, her end), HOUSE RULES (10: the offer as a numbered list with one rule for him). Leaders are 2 px and end in a 10 px open circle on metal, never on a stone. (4) THE F2 CARD on a cocoa #3B2620 scrim: logo_white 56 px, name Jost 500 26 px .2em, price Cormorant 56 px, one line Jost 26 px, offer box Jost 500 26 px .14em in a 2 px hairline with gold-light diamond separators; Feed y 880-1200, Story y 1000-1250; no CTA button in the image. A delivery line slot sits under the offer box, right-aligned, Jost 500 caps 20 px .14em bone at 80%, OFF by default (see changes). Type is drawn on the dark half of the frame; the splash, the milk crown and the piece are never lettered over.
camps.brandFeatures: The F2 card is the anchor on every card: Naira wordmark (logo_white, with its tulip I) on cocoa, name, price, one listing line, offer box 'BUY 2 · 10% OFF • BUY 3 · 20% OFF' (BUY3/BUY4 on card 8; on card 10 the house rules replace the box). Type is locked to Velista, Cormorant Garamond and Jost. The camp is a running joke on 'Petite': the whole game is finding something small in something big (a 10 mm charm in a 45 cm paraat), and the devices say so in millimetres. Hands carry mehendi and a red kalava, never another piece, so the Naira piece is the only jewellery in every frame. Sign-off on every ad, as the Meta description line and the carousel's last words: 'Naira Petite. Whoever finds it, keeps it.'
camps.palette: Plate: milk white, polished brass, blush and ivory petals (never on card 9), mehendi reddish-brown, red kalava. Grounds: oxblood #6E1F23 shamiana for the gold-tone and green pieces (cards 1, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10), plum #4A2540 for the rhodium Serpentine (card 6), milk white for the wire cam (card 2). Type: bone #F4F0E8 on dark, ink #1A1614 on milk; saffron #E8A33A for HER's tallies, the finish line and winning words on dark, coral-deep #C8664A on milk; terracotta #B5502F only for the live dot; gold-light #E4C889 for beats, hairline boxes and offer separators; cocoa #3B2620 under every card. The piece is always the most saturated or brightest thing in its frame: green on oxblood, clear on plum, gold on white, satin in lamplight.
camps.sellLever: BEST OF THREE is BUY3: the ritual's own rule is the offer, so cards 5 and 10 close on it and every primary text carries 'any three, 20% off with BUY3' before character 125. The ladder runs through the match: BUY3 on the trophy (5), BUY4 on 'best of four?' (8), where the bill shows Verdant Eternity Band ₹1,049 + Woven Gold Hoops ₹1,049 + Serpentine Whisper Chain — Silver ₹899 = ₹2,997, ₹2,398 with BUY3, and adding the ₹699 brushed earrings makes four pieces ₹2,587 with BUY4: the fourth piece adds about ₹190 (₹189.60 before rounding), which is the camp's sharpest reason to buy four; all three tiers as HOUSE RULES (10). Reason to buy now: this is the wedding week the pieces are shown surviving (haldi, sangeet, milk, day five), not a fake countdown. Funnel: PAIN 4, 7 · OUTCOME 2, 3, 9 · OBJECTION 1, 6 · OFFER 5, 8, 10; layers EDUCATION 2, 3 · TRUST 1, 4, 6, 7 · SELL 5, 8, 9, 10; cards 8 and 9 also run to men 18-24 as the gift. Stock logic: the anchors are the deepest slow stock (Woven 88, Verdant 58, Brushed 58, Triple Coil gold 20), while the thin pieces (Baroque Bloom 10, Tubogas gold 8, Droplet silver 11) sit on cards where one sale matters and nothing promises a count.
camps.carouselText: Angoothi dhoondhna, best of three: whoever finds the ring in the milk runs the house. Ten waterproof pieces went into the paraat and came out bright. Any three, 20% off with BUY3; any four, 30% off with BUY4. Naira Petite. Whoever finds it, keeps it.
camps.changes: Pushed the words from results to commentary: every Velista headline is now the broadcast's call and literally true of the piece. Card 2 'ROUND TWO: HERS AGAIN.' (samey with card 1) became 'VISIBLE FROM THE CHHAT.', the wire cam's boast and the outcome she wants. Card 3 'ALMOST TOUCHING.' collided with k10's card 10 and became 'TOO CLOSE TO CALL.', with a PHOTO FINISH device (a 1 px saffron finish line through the gap between the fingertips); the unlisted 'under 1 mm' gap is gone from the type, which now says 'almost touching' (the listing's words) and the listed 6.6 mm teardrop. Card 4 'NO STONES TO LOSE.' became 'NOTHING TO LOSE.' (the fearless team's phrase and the ring's bill of materials), with a sharper pain (a stone lost mid-sangeet, the baraat spent searching). Card 7 'FOUND: ONE SMALL CHARM.' became 'DAY FIVE. Background: deep oxblood velvet shamiana drape in soft vertical folds, far out of focus, with a few small warm fairy-light discs. The top quarter and the right third of the frame are calm dark oxblood for type. LIGHT: a warm amber rim light from behind left and a soft warm key from the front right; one small hard specular kicker gives every rib its own bright line and each pave stone a white catchlight. True contact where the coil meets the skin. Natural film grain, editorial demi-fine jewellery campaign quality. Only hands and forearms: no face, no eyes, no head. No text, letters, numbers or logos anywhere, nothing written in the mehendi. One piece of jewellery only, no star glints, no rainbow flare.

camps.name: MUJHE KUCH NAHI CHAHIYE.
camps.idea: Every Indian mother's yearly lie, set as type, and then corrected. One home at night under one tungsten bulb, hands and napes only, and in every frame the one bright thing she would never buy herself. Each card sets one of HER famous lines huge in bone Velista over the evidence of her life: 'Mujhe kuch nahi chahiye', 'Time kahan hai?', 'Mere paas sab hai', 'Baad mein pehnungi', and the lines that turn on the family ('Hilna mat, Mummy', 'Pehli salary, Maa', 'Ab tum bhi kehti ho', 'Bilkul Maa pe gayi hai'). Card 1 opens the camp with one terracotta stroke through NAHI, so her sentence finally says what she meant: MUJHE KUCH CHAHIYE. Down the left edge runs THE LADDER, a ledger of her years that every card re-tunes to its own proof: 32 years of the refusal, the plaits she fastened, the ring sizes she dodged, what she paid for him, her timetable, a leaning tower of steel katoris engraved with every occasion but hers, the 40 years Nani's necklace sat in the locker, two sisters saying the same thing. Every ladder breaks the same way, in terracotta: 2026, the piece's name, and some form of 'Order anyway.' The refusal is physical too: she lifts her thumbs to hand the hoops back, pushes the salary envelope across the table, and two sisters push one bracelet at each other. The offers climb like a ladder of their own: BUY 2 for the two sisters, BUY 3 for the three tiffin tiers, BUY 4 for Nani, Mummy, Mausi and you. The piece is always the only saturated thing in a cocoa frame, the grammar of both our tested winners. She saves every good thing for later; this one is made for a Tuesday.
camps.insight: She does not want nothing. Thirty years of putting herself last have turned 'no' into a reflex, and every good thing she owns is saved for later: the guest plates, the wedding silk, Nani's necklace in the locker. Arguing never works and asking never works (she will push it back across the table); a gift that is too practical to save does (waterproof, tarnish free, adjustable, made for a Tuesday), given anyway. And the 35-44 buyer has started saying the sentence herself, which turns one gift into a family order: two for the sisters, three with hers, four with Nani's.
camps.textualGraphic: (1) THE SENTENCE: her line in Velista caps, bone #F4F0E8, 104-132 px Feed and 120-150 px Story, 2 to 3 lines across the dark top third (x 330-1008, y 96-440), never digits, rupee, dots or dashes. When the line is spoken, an oversized Cormorant Garamond italic open quote in gold-light #E4C889 at 480-640 px hangs off the left edge behind the type at 70%. Under it a Jost 500 caps signature, 26 px tracked .16em (never under the 26 px floor), naming the speaker and when: 'MUMMY, EVERY YEAR SINCE 1994', 'YOU, AT 11 PM. SHE SAID IT FIRST.', 'NANI, ABOUT YOU'. Then the second beat in Cormorant italic 44-52 px gold-light. (2) THE STRIKE (card 1 only, the camp's opening move): a 10 px terracotta hand-cut stroke, rising 2 degrees left to right, through NAHI in the headline, so the line reads MUJHE KUCH CHAHIYE. It is the 2026 turn itself, which is why it may be terracotta. (3) THE LADDER: a narrow column on the left (x 72-300; Story y 290-990), set in Jost caps tracked .16em, fading from 15% at the top to 55-60% at the bottom like a till roll, each line with a 6 px perforation tick. It is a texture first and a text second, so its lines run under the 26 px floor (12-20 px); only its last line is read, and that line is always 30 px or more. Each card re-tunes it: the 32-line refusal (1994-2025); the fastenings (plaits, school tie, blouse hooks); her ring-size dodges; the kharcha ledger (dot leaders to 'MUMMY'); her own 12 years (2014-2025); her timetable (5:45 to 11:20, which dims when the last switch goes down); machine-engraved steel set on the rims of a katori tower (Jost 300, .3em, dotted underline); 40 locker dots, 4 filled; twin sister columns; mirrored mother-and-daughter columns facing across the cuff's gap. (4) THE BREAK: every ladder ends in terracotta #B5502F, '2026' in Jost 30 px, then the piece's name or the turn in Cormorant italic 30-36 px gold-light ('Woven Gold Hoops. Order anyway.', 'Her turn.', 'US 5 to 9. No need to ask.', 'Her time.', '2026 · ONE 18K GOLD TONE HEART · HERS'). Terracotta appears nowhere else: not on signatures, labels or beats. (5) THE DRAWN PROOF, grown from the ladder and drawn in gold-light hairlines over the picture, never generated: the quarter-turn diagram at the toggle, five US 5-9 gauge circles at true relative size around the ring (measured from the rendered ring, not assumed), the twelve-tick dial with no hands around the bangle ('NO HANDS. HERS ARE BUSY.'), the three tiffin tiers labelled MUMMY / MAUSI / TUM, kit callouts on the steel and the heart. Every drawn caption is Jost 26 px or more. (6) The F2 card on cocoa. Never more than four text elements: sentence set, ladder set, size or proof, card.
camps.brandFeatures: Palette: cocoa #3B2620 graded out of every picture, ink #1A1614 in the deepest shadows, bone type, gold-light for quote marks, beats and drawn proofs, terracotta for the 2026 turn only (the ladder's break and card 1's strike). Velista for her sentence, Cormorant italic for the beat, the break and the price, Jost for the ladder, signatures, labels and card. The F2 card on every ad, centred at the foot (Feed y 890-1200, Story y 1010-1250): the white Naira wordmark at 56 px with the tulip in the I, the name in Jost 500 caps 26 px .2em (card 4 prints BRUSHED 18K GOLD TONE EARRINGS, because the listing title's last word is banned in copy), the price in Cormorant 56 px (₹ from the Noto subset), one line in Jost 26 px, and the 2 px hairline offer box 'BUY 2 · 10% OFF ◆ BUY 3 · 20% OFF' in one 26 px line. The offer climbs across the camp: card 9 promotes BUY 2 (one for each sister), card 5 promotes BUY 3 (three tiers), card 10 promotes BUY 4 · 30% OFF (Nani, Mummy, Mausi, you). Footnote in Jost 26 px: the real size, CASH ON DELIVERY, IN THE NAIRA PETITE GIFT BOX; never free shipping (hard rule 5). The same grid on every ad (sentence top right, ladder left, piece centre right, card foot) makes it a series you recognise in one frame; card 10 breaks to symmetry to close it.
