In the pictures: one 2700K tungsten pool, the room near-monochrome umber, so the piece's metal or stones are the only saturated colour; card 3 sits on oxblood bedsheet, card 7 on black granite under a tower of steel, card 9 on a faded terracotta razai graded down to cocoa, card 5 is cool 7 am steel.
camps.sellLever: Emotional permission plus gift maths. 'Order anyway' answers the refusal, and the offers are cast as the family, climbing like the ladder: BUY 2 · 10% OFF is the two sisters who would each push the gift to the other (card 9); BUY 3 · 20% OFF is the three tiffin tiers, hers, Mausi's and yours (card 5), or Maa, Didi and Nani for the first-salary son (card 4); BUY 4 · 30% OFF is the whole line of women who say the sentence, Nani, Mummy, Mausi and you (card 10). Every primary text names BUY3 before character 125. Real baskets from this camp: Toggle ₹999 + Woven ₹1,049 + Triple Coil ₹1,149 = ₹3,197, ₹2,557.60 after 20%; Ribbon ₹699 + Brushed ₹699 + Heartbead ₹999 = ₹2,397, ₹1,917.60 after 20%; Torsade ₹1,099 + Verdant ₹1,049 + Toggle ₹999 + Ribbon ₹699 = ₹3,846, ₹2,692.20 after 30%. Against today's ₹1,153 average order that is 1.7 to 2.3x the basket; at the same cost per purchase, 2.2 x 2.3 is the road to ROAS 5. Cash on delivery lets the gift go straight to her door. Pre-order pieces (Molten Panel, Torsade) never promise dispatch.
camps.carouselText: Mummy has said 'Mujhe kuch nahi chahiye' every year since 1994. This year, cross out the nahi and order anyway. BUY2 = 10% off: one for each sister. BUY3 = 20% off: hers, Mausi's, yours. BUY4 = 30% off: add Nani. Cash on delivery, every piece in the Naira Petite gift box.
camps.changes: Kept the grid, the sentence, every ladder, cocoa and the F2 card; kept cards 2, 3, 5 and 8's pictures (already 10s). Pushed: (1) Card 1 gets the camp's signature type move: one terracotta stroke through NAHI, so her 32-year line reads MUJHE KUCH CHAHIYE; in motion her fingers close over the hoops as the stroke lands (she keeps them), and the 'prasad' framing is gone (puja-adjacent, founder-reject list). (2) Card 4 becomes a tug of love: her fingertips push the salary envelope back while his hand pushes it forward; beat '₹699. Push harder.' (3) Card 6 is now animated: she clicks off the house's last switch, the room drops to ink and only the bangle keeps the light while the timetable dims and the dial with no hands draws itself (4 animated: 1, 3, 5, 6). (4) Card 7's out-of-focus bowls become a leaning tower of twelve nested steel katoris rising out of frame, with the engraving ladder set on its rims, so the type and the photograph are one object. (5) Card 9 becomes two sisters each pushing the one bracelet at the other ('tu le le' / 'nahi, tu rakh'), which BUY 2 settles. (6) The offers now climb like a ladder: BUY 2 on card 9, BUY 3 on card 5, and card 10 promoted to BUY 4 · 30% OFF for Nani, Mummy, Mausi and you, the camp's biggest basket (₹2,692.20, 2.3x today's ₹1,153 order). Fixed against the hard rules: (7) '2026 · ONE GOLD HEART' said gold alone; now 'ONE 18K GOLD TONE HEART'. (8) Card 4's F2 name printed the listing title's banned last word; now BRUSHED 18K GOLD TONE EARRINGS. (9) Coin size referents dropped (coins are on the founder-reject list): thumb joint and thumb width instead. (10) Terracotta had leaked onto cards 3 and 5's signatures and a label; it is back to the 2026 turn only. (11) Every read line is 26 px or more (signatures were 24, footnotes and captions 22); only ladder texture runs under. (12) Card 8 no longer says the shell pearls themselves are tarnish free; the bracelet is. (13) Card 3's gauge is scaled from the rendered ring, because the model draws rings about 1.3x large. Still off: free shipping. The owner's ruling 6 says to print it, but hard rule 5 bans it and the checkout still charged ₹150 under ₹3,000 on 20 Nov (a BUY3 basket lands under it), so the footnote keeps CASH ON DELIVERY until checkout matches; the swap is one line. Heartbead (11) and Baroque (18) sit under 20 in stock: pause their ads if either sells out. truth: card 4's prompt had reworded the product card's lock, 'chunky huggie hoops', as 'chunky earrings'; the lock is pasted back word for word. The word sits only in the image prompt, where it keeps the hugging short-C shape, and stays out of every line of copy (the F2 name still prints BRUSHED 18K GOLD TONE EARRINGS). truth: card 10 printed 'PEARLS ABOUT 11 MM' in its footnote and size line. That is an estimate from the photos; the listing states only 17 cm end to end. The footnote now reads '17 CM END TO END · OPEN CUFF · CASH ON DELIVERY', and the size line keeps the card's own body referent, 'EACH PEARL ABOUT A FINGERNAIL WIDE'. All other checks passed on all 10 cards: every lock matches its card, with reference 1 named as the authority and the variants in stock; there is one product per picture; there are no faces or eyes, and every prompt bans generated text; there are no banned words, and claims appear only where tagged; there is no water for the toggle chain, the bangle, the shell bracelet or the cuff; prices are live and the BUY2/BUY3/BUY4 values are correct, with BUY3 inside the first 125 characters each time; there is no free shipping, compare-at or struck price; every size printed is listed; and the proof on the OBJECTION and TRUST cards is true.

ads.variant: Default Title, 18k gold tone (the only variant); show the pair.
ads.picture: Night, one bare tungsten bulb. A mother's two cupped hands (about 60, soft creases, a faint haldi stain on the right index fingertip, the faded indigo border of a cotton pallu across one wrist, no bangles or rings) held at chest height, palms up, her thumbs already lifting as if to hand the gift straight back. In the hollow: the pair of Woven Gold Hoops, one flat showing the chevron plait, one standing on edge with its 8 mm disc and latch catching the bulb. Far behind, almost black, one glint of the showcase glass where the good plates live. Over it her sentence, with one terracotta stroke through NAHI: MUJHE KUCH CHAHIYE. The gold is the only colour in a cocoa night.
ads.prompt: Vertical 9:16 editorial advertising photograph, a close still life of two cupped hands at night, seen from slightly above. Must stay a many-wire open braid, never a smooth tube, simple twist or oval. Do not redesign, restyle, resize or add anything. SCENE: the two cupped hands of an Indian woman of about sixty, held together at chest height, palms up, right hand slightly over the left, both thumbs lifted a little as if about to hand the gift back: warm wheatish-brown skin, soft creases, fine knuckle lines, short unpainted nails, five fingers with correct anatomy; a faint yellow haldi stain on the tip of the right index finger; the faded indigo border of a soft cotton sari pallu falls across her left wrist; the hands absolutely bare: no bangles, no rings, no mehendi, no thread, no watch, no other jewellery. In the hollow of her palms lies the pair: one hoop flat on her palm showing the chevron plait, the other standing on its edge against her fingers, the disc and latch toward the camera. SCALE: each hoop is 25 mm across, about as wide as the top joint of her thumb; the field of view across her palms is about 9 cm, so each hoop spans about a quarter of the frame width; a dark contact shadow where each hoop touches skin. Far behind, almost black, one glint of a glass showcase. COMPOSITION: the piece a little right of centre, one third to one half down the frame; the top third calm dark cocoa shadow for a headline; the left quarter calm shadow for a column of type; the lower 40% soft darkness for a card. LIGHT: one bare warm tungsten bulb above left, soft, falling off fast into shadow; one small hard specular kicker from behind right draws a crisp pure-white highlight along every polished wire of the braid. GRADE: deep warm cocoa and umber, near-monochrome; the 18k gold tone is the only bright, saturated thing, warm-neutral yellow, never orange or brassy. Natural film grain, believable imperfection, the hush of an Indian home at night. No face, no eyes, no lips. No text, letters, numbers, logos or printing on anything. One product only: no other jewellery anywhere in the frame.

ads.motion: Kling 3.0, 5 s, from the still: a slow 3% push-in; the bulb's cord sways a few millimetres so the warm pool of light drifts across her palms; at 2.5 s one specular glint travels along the braid of the standing hoop; at 3.6 s her lifted thumbs lower and her fingers curl inward a few millimetres, cradling the hoops instead of handing them back (never covering them): she keeps them. ads.risk: Extra jewellery on her hands (generators add bangles and a ring to an Indian woman's hands), the open braid smoothing into a plain twisted tube, and the lifted thumbs turning into a clumsy six-finger knot. Hedge take: palms open flat side by side, thumbs relaxed, both hoops lying down.
ads.why10: The truest sentence in Indian family life, corrected with one terracotta stroke: the scroller reads 'Mujhe kuch nahi chahiye' in her mother's voice and, a beat later, 'Mujhe kuch chahiye', which is what she always meant. It is an editorial device no Indian jewellery brand has used; the 32-year till roll makes the cost visible, the waterproof fact arrives as her own question, and in motion her fingers close over the hoops as the stroke lands.

camps.name: PARCHHAI.
camps.textualGraphic:
The type system is THE DOUBLE LINE. The headline obeys the same sun as the photograph, down to the light that slips through.

1. OBJECT LINE (in the light).
   - Type: Velista caps, 124-132 px on Feed and 132 px on Story, tracking .02em, ligatures off.
   - Colour: ink #1A1614 on sky, pista and saffron walls; bone #F4F0E8 on terracotta, coral-deep and plum.
   - Content: an honest count, such as 'TWO STONES.' Card 9 alone counts the light: 'ONE MOON.'
   - Position: x 72, from Feed y 128 (y 150 under a kicker) or Story y 290, in the calm sunlit upper left. It never touches the silhouette.

2. TYPE-SHADOW (the meaning). It hangs directly under the object line from its baseline.
   - Type: Cormorant Garamond italic 500, lowercase, about 0.7x the cap size (80-96 px).
   - Colour: cocoa #3B2620, mix-blend-mode multiply, 55% on light walls and 72% on dark walls.
   - Transform: transform-origin top left, skewX(22deg) scaleY(1.18), so it leans the way the plate's shadows lean. The designer measures the plate's lean and uses it in place of 22. Mirror the skew if the sun is on the right.
   - Built like real sun from two stacked copies. Copy A is sharp and masked to its top 40% (the contact). Copy B is blur(3px) and masked to its lower 60% (the penumbra).
   - Width: 1.0-1.8x the object line's width, because a low sun's shadow is longer than what casts it. Wrap to two lines inside 936 px.

3. THE LIGHT IN THE TYPE. Where the plate lets light through its shadow, the type does too.
   - Style: bone #F4F0E8 at 85%, mix-blend screen, 8 px warm glow, at the same skew, never gold-light.
   - Card 1: the word 'aur' is lit (the crystal's caustic glows where the two figures' hands meet).
   - Card 4: the dot of the i in 'nagamani' is lit (the jewel in the cobra's hood).
   - Card 10: the three branch labels are lit (the green light in the canopy; set in bone, not green).
   - Card 9 is the only line set wholly in light (item 8).
   - Two more physical jokes:
     - On card 2 the letters of 'titliyan.' lift off the baseline one by one, as if following the butterfly.
     - On card 8 the space between 'bhi' and 'paas' is exactly the width of the hands' gap in frame.

4. THE SUN.
   - A 14 px filled dot sits on the frame edge where a line drawn back from the piece along the measured sun angle leaves the frame.
   - Beside it, a Jost 500 26 px caps label (tracking .14em) gives the hour, for example '4:52 PM · 21 DEC'.
   - One 1.5 px hairline ray (ink or bone at 45%) runs from the dot to the piece's brightest specular point. It ends in the kit's 10 px open circle, on metal, never on a stone.
   - The hours and the sun's true height advance card by card: carousel A runs 3:58 to 4:52 PM; carousel B runs 4:02 to 5:21 PM, LAST LIGHT.

5. SIZE LINE AT THE ROOT.
   - Type: Jost 500 26 px caps, tracking .12em.
   - Position: under the piece on the ledge face, or beside it on the wall for worn cards.
   - It sits over a 1.5 px dimension bracket with 12 px end ticks that spans the piece's true outline in frame.
   - When the verified plate shows 19 or more Feed px per listed mm, the line opens with 'SHOWN MAGNIFIED ·' (likely only card 9).
   - The joke grows from 'SHADOW NOT INCLUDED' through 'SECRETS', 'BHAIYA' and 'THE OTHER 1,740 KM' to 'GARDEN NOT INCLUDED'. It flips once, on the moon card: 'MOON INCLUDED · STARS NEXT DECEMBER'.
   - A line over 44 characters breaks into two lines at a ' · '.

6. A DEVICE FOR EACH ANGLE.
   - OUTCOME: the shadow alone carries the feeling; nothing is added.
   - PAIN: a Jost 500 26 px caps kicker above the object line names the pain in the buyer's own words: 'SECRET SANTA. ₹1,000 LIMIT.' / 'SHE'S IN BENGALURU. YOU'RE IN DELHI.' / 'FIRST DECEMBER TOGETHER. ZERO IDEAS.' The shadow shows the piece ending it.
   - OBJECTION and TRUST: sun-ray callouts, as in an architect's sciagraphy (the drawing of shadows).
     - Up to two hairline rays run parallel to the sun ray. Each ends in a 10 px open circle on metal and carries a kit callout (Jost 500 26 px caps over one Jost 400 26 px line) with a listing fact. The proof arrives along the light.
     - On Feed the callouts replace the F2 card's line.
     - On Story the callouts drop and the card line returns. OBJECTION cards then gain a kicker that asks the objection outright: 'IS ONE BANGLE ENOUGH?' / 'GOLD TONE OR SILVER TONE?'
   - OFFER: the thread (item 7) and the BUY3 box.

7. THE THREAD ('A SENTENCE IN THREE PIECES').
   - Cards 3, 4 and 5 end their type-shadows with semicolons, so a swipe reads one sentence that names three people: 'a whole stack, for didi; / the nagamani, for you; / and the whole sangeet, for the cousin.'
   - Card 5 completes the sentence and lands the offer.
   - On card 10 the sentence lives in the tree as three Cormorant italic 44 px bone labels on three branch tips: 'nani se,' / 'maa tak,' / 'mujh tak.'

8. THE INVERSION (card 9), the only type-light. The meaning line is bone at 85% with mix-blend screen and a 10 px warm glow, skewed the same way, because on this card the piece throws light.

9. TYPE IN MOTION (cards 1, 2, 5 and 9).
   - The type-shadow begins as the object line's own true shadow: the same capitals in cocoa, short and skewed.
   - As the plate's shadow stretches into its meaning, the type-shadow lengthens and re-letters, glyph by glyph, into the meaning line.
   - It finishes a beat after the picture: the lit word or the last semicolon lands last.
   - On card 9 there is no shadow to start from, so the type-light rises with the moon.

RULES ACROSS ALL CARDS
- Gold-light #E4C889 never appears in type. It belongs to the lit side of the metal. The one exception is the kit's lozenge in the offer box on dark walls.
- Type budget per card: kicker or callouts, object line, type-shadow, sundial label, size line, then the F2 card. Never more.
- Never type over skin, the piece or the silhouette.
- Velista lines carry no digits and no ₹. Numbers live in Jost: the kicker, sundial, size line and card.
camps.brandFeatures:
WORDMARK AND F2 CARD
- The Naira wordmark lives only in the F2 card, at 56 px (kit .card .wm): ink on light walls, bone on dark. The top band belongs to the sun and the headline, so there is no second wordmark.
- The F2 card contains:
  - the wordmark;
  - the name in Jost 26 px caps .2em;
  - the price in Cormorant 56 px;
  - one Jost 26 px line of listing facts;
  - the offer box as one 26 px line: 'CODE BUY2 · 10% OFF ◆ BUY3 · 20% OFF'. The codes are not automatic, so the box says CODE.
- On the BUY3 cards, a Cormorant italic 44 px line sits above the box and the box text changes:
  - Card 5: line 'Three people. Three things you never said.'; box 'THREE PEOPLE ◆ CODE BUY3 · 20% OFF'.
  - Card 10: line 'Three generations, one order. Nani's first, obviously.'; box 'THREE GENERATIONS ◆ CODE BUY3 · 20% OFF'.
- Position: centred at Feed y 930-1230 and Story y 1010-1250. On worn cards it is left- or right-aligned so it never crosses skin.

PLACEMENT (19 Nov ruling)
- The Feed is the 4:5 window chosen per plate with .pic object-position (default: plate y 200-1550). The Story is the native frame.
- Placement gate for this camp: the piece's full extent sits inside Feed y 380-930. Its meaning-shadow may rise above y 380 only in the right half (x 540 and right), never into the headline column.

TYPE AND COLOUR
- Three type families only:
  - Velista for the object lines;
  - Cormorant Garamond italic for the type-shadows, beats and prices;
  - Jost for the sundial, size line, kicker, callouts and card.
- Every wall is a palette token rendered as lime-wash, and every shadow is cocoa #3B2620, so ten walls read as one family. Gold-light is reserved for the lit side of the metal.

VOICE
- Object lines are 2-5 words ending in a full stop, and every one is a count.
- Kickers quote the buyer's own December: a budget limit, a city, a first. They never use adjectives.
- At most one Hindi phrase per card, one an urban reader needs no gloss for. The brand's own proven 'Tum aur main.' leads.
- The pace is 'Softly, slowly, worn.': the slowest afternoon of the year.

THE SERIES
- The ownable, screenshot-able device is the size line, '... NOT INCLUDED'. It escalates card by card and flips once, on the moon.
- The ownable motion is the shadow growing while the piece stays still, while the type's own shadow re-letters into its meaning.
- The sundial label is the campaign's clock. A viewer who sees two cards learns that the afternoon is running out.
- Carousel link headlines use the object line in sentence case plus the price ('Two stones. ₹899').

camps.sellLever:
NOW
- 21 December is the winter solstice, with the longest shadows of the year. The camp runs through December, and the sundial hours make the date the campaign's own clock.
- December is the month she buys for everyone at once: weddings and sangeet, Christmas, the office Secret Santa, New Year, the cousins.

WHO EACH PIECE IS FOR: each slow piece arrives with one person and one sentence, so the ad answers 'what do I give whom' before she asks. Nine people, with no repeats outside the thread.
| Recipient | Piece | The pain or wish it answers |
|---|---|---|
| Him or her | Halo Curve | tum aur main: two that don't match |
| Herself | Lilac Papillon, Serpentine | the one she keeps for herself |
| Didi | Triple Coil | 'is one bangle enough?' |
| The cousin | Woven | the whole sangeet |
| The office Secret Santa | Toggle | a ₹1,000 limit; the Toggle is ₹999 |
| The new bhabhi | Duo Link | you don't know yet if she wears gold tone or silver tone |
| The one in another city | Droplet cuff | she's in Bengaluru, you're in Delhi |
| The girlfriend (for men 18-24) | Bold Dome | first December together, zero ideas |
| Nani, maa and you | Verdant, three of them | one adjustable ring that fits all three |

BUY3 LOGIC: the gift list is the bundle, and the bundle is the ROAS lever. These pieces sit at ₹899-1,299, so BUY3 roughly triples the basket in one checkout. That is the realistic road from 2.2 toward 5.
- Every primary text carries 'Any three pieces, 20% off with BUY3' before character 125.
- Cards 5 and 10 carry the camp lines 'Three people. Three things you never said.' and 'Three generations, one order. Nani's first, obviously.'
- The carousel A thread names a ready trio: Triple Coil for didi + Serpentine for you + Woven for the cousin. That is ₹3,497 before BUY3, about ₹2,798 after (planning maths only, never printed).
- Card 10 sells three of a kind: three Verdant bands, ₹3,147 before BUY3. The US 5 to 9 fit is the reason one ring works for three hands.
- Card 6 sells under a price ceiling: ₹999 under the ₹1,000 Secret Santa limit. Its primary text still carries BUY3, for the rest of the list.
- BUY4 for long lists: 'Four on the list? 30% off with BUY4.'

9:16 macro on a Jodhpur sky-blue lime-washed terrace wall at 3:58 PM on 21 Dec, sun 16 degrees up.

- Its shadow rises up the wall to the right. For a few millimetres it is the ring; then it becomes two people side by side, leaning in and holding hands. The stones are their heads; the band's two passing ends are their joined hands.

ads.motion:
Kling 3.0, 5 s, camera locked. Start and end frames are made from the same plate.
- START: an edit of the plate in which the shadow is only the ring's true outline, short and low on the wall.
- END: the final plate.

Timeline:
- 0-1.5 s: dust motes drift in the sunbeam; the light warms and drops a little lower.
- 1.5-3.5 s: the shadow stretches up the wall and leans apart into two figures.
- 3.5-4.2 s: their hands meet.
- 4.2-5 s: the champagne caustic slides from the crystal's shadow into the joined hands.

The ring and ledge never move, morph or rescale; a pixel-locked mask in the edit holds them.

Type in the edit (the camp's signature move):
- At 0 s the type-shadow is the object line's own true shadow: 'TWO STONES.' in cocoa caps, short and skewed.
- As the plate's shadow stretches, the type-shadow lengthens and re-letters, glyph by glyph, into 'tum aur main.'
- 'aur' lights last, at 4.6 s, as the caustic reaches the hands.
- The sundial counts 3:41 to 3:58 PM.

Sound: terrace room tone, a pigeon's wings, one soft tabla tap when the hands meet.
ads.risk:
Two risks:
- the tiger eye drifting glassy or into a second crystal (the card's main morph);
- the model drawing a real couple, or a cut-out, behind the ring.
Standing the ring upright also risks the placement gate (b03-3 failed on extent), so check the extent before anything else.

Hedge take:
1. Generate the same plate with only the ring's true short shadow and a clean wall.
2. Build the two figures as an SVG cocoa multiply silhouette rooted in the traced ring shadow.
3. Give it a blur ramp from 0 px at the ring to 6 px at the heads, and multiply the plaster texture through it.
4. Add a champagne radial glow where the hands meet.
ads.why10: It is the most legible shadow in the set: two people holding hands reads in a tenth of a second. It carries the brand's own proven line 'Tum aur main.' The physics rewards a second look: the clear stone lets the sun through and the opaque one does not. Now even the type obeys it, because only the word 'and' is lit.

camps.name: UDHAAR KHATA.
camps.idea: WORLD: night, and every frame is a flash photograph of a small family crime. In an Indian home jewellery is on permanent loan, and Didi keeps the account in a red cloth bahi-khata: who took what, for which function, and whether it came back. Each card is shot the way a crime, a party or a wedding is shot, with a hard on-camera flash and a crisp black drop shadow, and each is a different kind of evidence: the clean ring a lifted hoop left in spilled talc, a chain escaping a shut potli in a moving auto while the city streaks, a mehendi hand posing a ring at a sangeet, a pair standing either side of the brass line of an Art Deco floor, a wrist laid across the closed red ledger, an ear leaving through the front door, a toggle in a frozen shower of mandap petals, a ring on a sizing mandrel in an emptied tray, a birthday box being robbed, three palms waiting for their share. The headline is always the excuse, quoted back in Velista (SIRF EK FUNCTION KE LIYE.), and Didi's torn ledger strip runs under every frame, its WAPAS column filling with ?, ?? and ???. Each card adds one document Didi would really use to chase the piece, born from the picture and carrying real listing facts: a date imprint that rolls from the 2nd to the 20th, a tear-off pad where every page says KAL, a missing report with a reward, a layout that is the earring's own face, the closing double rule, a library issue card with a waiting list, an identification sketch, a ring-size ruler of family members, a gift tag, masking-tape name labels. THE ARC: cards 1-4 are the crimes and the excuses; card 5 closes the books (the question marks turn into ticks because Didi bought everyone their own); cards 6-9 are the repeat offenders; card 10 is the joint-family settlement. The only way to close the account is to buy three: one for you, one for her, one for whoever she lends it to. RULES: borrowers are family roles only, never names; every word is HTML and the pictures carry none; no faces; no water anywhere; hands appear on only five cards (3, 5, 6, 9, 10) and wear nothing but chipped plum polish, a hair tie or mehendi.
camps.insight: In an Indian family no piece of jewellery belongs to one woman. It goes out 'sirf ek function ke liye' and comes back never, and every sister has both said and heard the excuses. Wedding season is when it peaks: five functions, three cousins, one good pair of earrings. So BUY3 is not a discount here; it is the only known way to get your own earrings back.
camps.textualGraphic: THE EXCUSE, THE KHATA, THE STAMP, plus one document per card. (1) THE EXCUSE: a terracotta #B5502F Cormorant Garamond open quote at 320 px hangs at the top-left margin (Feed x 44, y 18; Story y 250), and the borrower's line sits inside it in Velista caps, bone #F4F0E8, 96-150 px, line-height .96, max 3 lines, left-aligned at x 132: Didi quoting it back. On card 5 the quote closes; on card 9, where Didi herself speaks, it turns oxblood. (2) THE ATTRIBUTION BEAT: Cormorant italic 500, 34-40 px, gold-light #E4C889, set like a court record: '— Chhoti, 2 Nov. The function was on the 4th. Today is the 20th.' (3) THE KHATA STRIP across the lower third (Feed y 930-1266; Story y 980-1250, never below): a torn strip of ledger page in bone with 5% warm paper noise, deckled top and bottom edges cut by an SVG path, rotated -1.5° and bleeding off both sides; sky #9EC3D6 rules every 42 px at 45%; a double terracotta margin (2 px + 2 px, 6 px apart) at x 170; an oxblood #6E1F23 cloth spine 64 px wide down the left edge with a bone SVG running stitch (dash 10/8). Never more than 3 rows; cards 6 and 8 drop the rows because their device is the record. Some cards rename a column (KISKE SAATH, or the missing report's RANG · NISHAAN · NAAP · AAKHRI BAAR DEKHA). Its word changes every card: WAPAS NAHI AAYA, YAAD DILAYA, DEKHA GAYA, PENDING, KHATA BAND, WAITING LIST, PEHCHAAN LIYA, SIZE: SAB KA, BAAKI, KHATA BAND. (5) THE F2 CARD on the strip's right page (Feed x 650-1008): Naira wordmark (logo_ink) 48 px, name Jost 500 22 px .2em caps, price Cormorant 500 54 px ink with the ₹ from the Noto subset, one line Jost 22 px, offer box Jost 500 22 px .14em caps in a 2 px ink border; Story condenses to a 40 px wordmark and 46 px price. (6) THE SIZE LINE: Jost 500 22 px caps .12em bone in a 2 px bone frame pinned beside the piece; real mm always, 'SHOWN MAGNIFIED' whenever the frame runs above 19 px per mm. (7) ONE DOCUMENT PER CARD, taken from the picture: 1 a saffron seven-segment date imprint burned into the evidence, which rolls like an odometer from 2 11 26 to 20 11 26 in the animated cut, plus a terracotta dashed circle round the empty print, 'yahan thi'; 2 a tear-off pad whose every page says KAL; 3 a GUMSHUDA KI TALAASH missing report with kit callouts on the S-wave and an INAAM (reward) line that is the offer; 4 the whole layout as the earring's face, black half, gold rule, white half, with the headline and beat changing colour mid-word as they cross the rule; 5 the books closed with ticks and an accountant's double rule; 6 a manila issue card stamped with borrowers' dates and BOOKED, ending in Didi's pencil note 'ya apne le lo'; 7 Didi's ballpoint identification sketch of the toggle with callouts; 8 a ruler of US 5 to 9 laid along the ring mandrel, one family member per size; 9 a die-cut gift tag, TO: me, FROM: me, NOW WITH: Chhoti; 10 masking-tape name labels on three palms. Piece and words lock together: the stamp always lands on the offer, the strip's last WAPAS entry always points at the piece, and no device ever covers the piece. Every word is HTML.
camps.brandFeatures: The Naira wordmark heads the strip's right page the way a stationer's name is printed on a khata, and the stamp's ring reads NAIRA PETITE · DIDI KA KHATA, so the brand is the ledger Didi keeps. The F2 card closes every frame (wordmark, name, ₹ price, one line, offer box) on the bone right page, with the terracotta stamp biting the offer. Kit type only: Velista for the excuses (caps, no digits, no ₹), Cormorant italic for the beats, the ledger entries, the ✓ and ? marks and the prices, Jost for column heads, labels, stamps, size lines and the offer. Palette tokens only. The series look is three things you can spot at 200 px: the flash with its black shadow, the torn bone strip with the oxblood spine, and the slanted terracotta stamp. No free-shipping footer, no struck prices, no reviews.
camps.palette: Flash-black ink #1A1614 graded to oxblood #6E1F23 at the frame edges (the ledger's cloth); bone #F4F0E8 for the strip, the tags and the cards; terracotta #B5502F for the open quote, the stamp and the ? and ✓ marks; sky #9EC3D6 for the faint ledger rules; gold-light #E4C889 only on the beats and the price; ink for entries; plum #4A2540 echoed by the borrower's chipped nail polish; saffron #E8A33A only for card 1's date imprint. Inside the pictures the grounds are deep and saturated (talc-dusted walnut, black vinyl and sodium streaks, plum satin, henna, black and white honed stone, red ledger cloth, oxblood door, magenta silk and red petals, oxblood velvet, cocoa falloff) so every piece, gold tone or rhodium silver tone, is the brightest thing in its frame. Never pale on pale.
camps.sellLever: 'Buy three, get yours back.' BUY3 = 20% off three or more pieces, and the camp makes three the natural number: one for you, one for her, one for whoever she lends it to. Every card carries the offer box BUY 3 · 20% OFF ◆ ONE EACH under a stamp; cards 5 and 10 close the account (BUY 3 · 20% OFF ◆ KHATA BAND). Every primary text says 'Any three, 20% off with BUY3' before character 125. Why now: wedding season is when the borrowing happens, and the two ₹699 pieces (Ribbon Bead, Brushed Gold) make a three-piece order easy. Slow pieces get a reason to be wanted: each is the thing someone in the family would not give back. Routing for the ₹5,000/day CBO: PAIN ad set cards 1, 2, 9; OBJECTION 3, 4, 8; OUTCOME 6, 7; OFFER 5, 10. Retargeting: TRUST 3 and 6, SELL 5 and 10. Cards 1-5 run first, 6-10 second. No fake urgency, no struck or compare-at prices, no free shipping.
camps.carouselText: Every family has a borrower, and every Didi keeps a khata. Close yours: any three, 20% off with BUY3. One for you, one for her, one for whoever she lends it to.
camps.changes: Kept the world, the excuses, the product order, the BUY3 logic, the arc and the graphic system (excuse, khata strip, stamp, one document per card), and pushed every card that was safe, samey or risky. THE BIG ONE: five of the ten pictures used the same gesture (plum fingertips reaching in from the right). Now only five cards have hands at all, and each picture is a different kind of evidence. (1) Card 1, PAIN: the hand lifting a hoop became the scene of the crime. One hoop lies in spilled talc beside the clean bare ring its twin left, with the borrower's hair tie as the clue. The absence sells the pain at 200 px. The date imprint now reads 20 11 26, and in the animated cut it rolls like an odometer from the 2nd to the 20th. A dashed terracotta circle marks the print: 'yahan thi'. (2) Card 2, PAIN: the clutch and fingertips became a getaway. A chain escapes a shut plum potli in a moving auto, shot with flash plus a slow shutter, so the barrel freezes while the city streaks. The barrel now hangs at the bottom of a U-loop, where gravity really puts it. New beat: 'The potli came back on the 9th. Empty.' (3) Card 3, OBJECTION: the missing report gains an INAAM (reward) line, and the reward is the offer. (4) Card 4, OBJECTION: the floor now splits left and right, black | brass | white, so the frame is the hoop's own face, and each hoop stands on its opposite colour. ads.motion: Kling 3.0, 5 s, camera locked with a 3% push-in toward the print. 0.0-0.2 s: the flash blows the frame to white and falls back to the flash-lit exposure; at 0.4 s a second, smaller pop (Didi takes another for the file). ads.risk: The print. Models may skip the bare ring, draw it as a raised ring of powder instead of a void, or put a second hoop into it, and the flash can blow the talc white and flatten the rope ridges. Gate on one hoop, one hoop-sized bare ring, a dark readable ground and every ridge. Hedge take: the caught-in-the-act frame, the twin lifted between two plum-polished fingers.
ads.why10: The crime is told by an absence: one gold hoop and the clean ring its twin left in the talc, with the borrower's hair tie as the clue. At 200 px it reads as gold and void, thing and missing thing, before a word is read, which is the oldest trick in great print advertising (show the hole, not the object). The date imprint rolling from the 2nd to the 20th makes the lie visible in time, and the BUY3 line is the punchline, not a discount.

camps.name: BIJLI GAYI.
camps.idea:
WORLD: one power cut in a shaadi-season house, logged minute by minute from 8:41 PM to 9:31 PM, and lit by ten different lights, every one of which an Indian has used in the dark. Each card is a different room, a different thing Indians really do, and a different light, so each card is a different test of the finish:
- 8:41, CHAANDNI: the drawing-room switch. The fan winds down, the house says 'ohhh', and only the moon comes in through the window grille.
- 8:42, MAACHIS: the kitchen shelf, where the matchbox is found.
- 8:47, TORCH: mehendi night, where a torch inspects the earrings.
- 8:55, 200 PHONES: the shamiana. The generator dies mid-sangeet, the crowd raises its phone torches, and she is mid 'bulb lagao' step.
- 9:03, PADOSI KA SCOOTER: the stairwell. The bulbs are gone from their holders and a neighbour's headlight slants in.
- 9:10, EMERGENCY LIGHT: the dressing room, where the make-up artist's ring light dies an hour before the photos.
- 9:14, LALTEN: a hand makes the swan on the wall.
- 9:20, MOMBATTI: the table becomes the first candlelight dinner in fifteen years.
- 9:26, DIYA: the candles have burnt down and only the diya is left.
- 9:31, MAINS: the inverter beeps, the lights return and she walks in.

Cards 1-9 are dark. Card 10 is the only lit frame, so the carousel ends with the lights coming on.

In every frame the piece is the brightest, most saturated thing. That is the grammar both our static winners obeyed. Every frame also has an honest referent in the room: a 45 mm switch, a 52 mm matchbox, a mehendi cone, a wrist, a 35 mm bulb holder, a thumb, a little finger, an ear, a 20 mm candle.

The darkness is a real demonstration of finish, and ten lights make it ten tests:
- polish throws pinpoints;
- pavé throws a scatter;
- a rivière throws a ring of ovals;
- a cushion stone holds its green under a torch and throws it on the silk;
- a braid gives every wire its own highlight;
- satin glows instead of flashing.

GRAPHIC SYSTEM:
- 'LIT TYPE': the Velista headline is lit by the piece through a radial mask, with its floor raised to 55% so every letter still reads at 200 px. Four cards break the rule on purpose: card 3 is lit by the torch's hard circle, card 4 is half dead and half lit, card 9 is dimmed and card 10 is fully lit.
- THE LOG: a saffron seven-segment time readout drawn in SVG, like the inverter's display, plus a Jost line that names the light: 'PM · BIJLI GAYI · ROSHNI: MAACHIS'.
- The second beat is in the piece's own sampled colour.
- The Indian SWITCHBOARD is the camp's spec device: down is ON, a saffron neon indicator, masking-tape labels.
- Exactly one device born from each room: the ember question mark, the torch-test inset, the enlarged switchboard, the socket tags, the fifteen-cup ring, the outline traced from the piece, the RESERVED table card, the fan-regulator dial and the all-on switchboard.
- The spray of light is an After Effects/SVG layer whose dots take the shape of each piece's cut. It stays on walls and props, is never generated and never sits on the piece.

GRAFT (type-2 DO MATLAB): card 10, 'BIJLI AAYI.', means both 'the power is back' and 'the stunner walked in'.

RULES:
- Ten cards, ten different light sources. No candle before 8:42, because nobody has found the maachis yet.
- No flame, bulb or lamp in frame brighter than the piece.
- No water anywhere.
- No mirrors, faces or profiles: ears from behind, hands and forearms only.
- No star glints.
- No branded inverter, ring light, emergency lamp, lantern, generator, scooter or phone.
- No text in the plates.
- The Prism's light stays lilac, pink, lemon and white.
camps.insight: Darkness is the one honest test of how jewellery handles light, and every Indian has sat in it and can name its ten lights: the moon through the window grille, 'maachis kahan hai?', the torch, the crowd's phone torches, the neighbour's scooter sweeping the stairwell, the emergency light, the lalten and its shadow animals, the candle on an upturned katori, the last diya, and then the inverter beep and 'light aa gayi!'. Each of those lights shows something different about a finish: polish throws pinpoints, pavé a scatter, satin a glow, a clear stone throws its colour. So the country's most shared domestic joke becomes ten product demonstrations. It sits inside the frame our data says sells: one piece, the brightest and most saturated thing, on a dark ground. And wedding season is when the lights fail: dim shamianas, dead generators, ring lights that die before the photos. For the 35-44 buyer the memory is exact. She grew up doing homework by lalten and making swans on the wall, and fifteen years into marriage a power cut is the only candlelight dinner she gets.
camps.textualGraphic:
LIT TYPE
- The H1 is Velista caps in bone #F4F0E8, 104-190 px Feed (100-180 px Story), leading .96, tracking .02em, no digits.
- The piece lights it. A CSS radial-gradient mask, centred on the jewel's measured pixel position, holds the letters at 100% within 300 px of the jewel and fades them to 55% at 900 px. The words nearest the piece glow and the far ends sink into the room, but every letter still reads on a 200 px thumbnail. (The floor was 20%, which lost the far words at phone size.)
- It never sits on a panel or a scrim; it sits in the room's dark.
- Four exceptions carry meaning:
  - Card 3, 'TORCH MAAR KE DEKHO.', is lit by a hard torch circle instead of a soft falloff: letters inside a 330 px circle centred on the torch spot are at 100%, and letters outside are at 50%. The hard edge cuts across the second line mid-letter, as if the torch swept up over the words.
  - Card 4 is half dead and half lit: 'GENERATOR GAYA.' is bone at 50% with no glow, and 'BULB LAGAO.' is gold-light at 100% with a glow. The pain and the answer are told in type.
  - Card 9, 'DHEEMI ROSHNI.', is the one dimmed headline: bone at 62% with a 26 px gold-light halo. It glows; it does not shine.
  - Card 10, 'BIJLI AAYI.', is the one fully lit headline: no falloff, a saffron glow, and it switches on letter by letter in the Reel.
- Card 2's '?' has a burnt match head for its dot (SVG, saffron core into terracotta, 10 px glow, a 1 px wisp of smoke), the only lit thing in that headline.

SECOND BEAT
- Cormorant Garamond italic 500, 38-44 px.
- Set in the piece's own colour sampled from the plate: gold-light #E4C889 for 18k gold tone, rhodium white #EEF2F5, a three-stop lilac #B9A0E0 / pink #F0AACB / lemon #EEDF7E grade for the Prism, the cushion's green (about #4FB383), the heart's icy blue (about #A9DBEA). Card 10 uses terracotta on the lit room.

THE LOG
- Top left of every card, a seven-segment time readout drawn in SVG (38 px tall, 3 px segments), saffron #E8A33A at 85% with its unlit segments at 8%, like the display on an Indian inverter or a digital wall clock. It is an illustration, not a font, so no digits ever enter Velista.
- Beside it, on the same baseline, a Jost 500 caps line, 20 px, .16em, bone at 60%: 'PM · BIJLI GAYI · ROSHNI: <the light>'.
- Ten cards, one fifty-minute power cut, ten lights: CHAANDNI, MAACHIS, TORCH, 200 PHONES, PADOSI KA SCOOTER, EMERGENCY LIGHT, LALTEN, MOMBATTI, DIYA, MAINS. The light is named because each light is the test.
- The readout dims to 45% on card 9 (the inverter is running low). On card 10 it turns ink on the lit room and the line reads 'BIJLI AAYI · ROSHNI: MAINS'.

THE SWITCHBOARD
- An ivory bone plate (SVG, 440x92 px, 6 px radius, 1 px #3B3430 hairline) of piano rocker switches, drawn the Indian way:
  - ON: the lower half is pressed in, and a 10 px saffron #E8A33A neon indicator glows beside it.
  - OFF: the upper half is pressed and the indicator is dead #3B3430.
- Above each rocker, a strip of masking tape (torn-edge SVG, #E9DFC6, rotated 1.5-3°) carries a Jost 500 caps label in ink, 19 px .1em, the way Indian homes label their boards.
- Labels: 'BIJLI' (off), then the piece's truth (on): 'TOGGLE', '6 PEARLS', 'HARA', 'PAVÉ LINK', '15 CUPS', 'NO CLASP', 'NEELA', 'WATERPROOF'.
- It replaces the F2 card's text line. On card 10 every rocker is down and the last tape reads 'BUY3 · 20% OFF'.

LIGHT DOTS
- An After Effects/SVG layer drawn over the plate, only on walls, cloth and props, never on the piece.
- 15-80 soft dots: radius 3-14 px, blur 2-5 px, 25-70% opacity, screen blend.
- Each dot takes the shape of the cut:
  - pinpoints for polish;
  - tiny squares on point and short bars for the Prism's princess and baguette cuts;
  - a radial sunburst of round pinpoints for the Verdant's halo;
  - soft ovals for the rivière;
  - navettes for the marquise;
  - one round icy spot for the heart.
- No dots on the brushed satin card (one soft radial glow instead), the phone-bokeh card or the lit card.
- Card 5 adds faint dashed SVG bulb outlines under its two empty holders: the ghosts of the bulbs still to come.
- No four-point star glints anywhere.

SIZE TAPE
- Only where a plate passes 19 Feed px per listed mm (px per mm = 1080 / field of view in mm), a strip of masking tape near the piece carries Jost 500 caps 22 px 'SHOWN MAGNIFIED · ...'. Below that, the tape prints the listed size plainly. None of the ten plates pass 19 px (cards 2 and 3 were wrongly tagged 'shown magnified' at 13.5 and 15 px per mm), so every size tape in this camp is a plain size line.

ONE ROOM DEVICE PER CARD, NEVER TWO
- 1: the switchboard in the F2 line ('BIJLI' off, 'TOGGLE' on).
- 2: the ember question mark.
- 3: torch-test inset (a real 3× crop of the plate, with leaders ending on metal).
- 4: enlarged switchboard (GENERATOR, DJ, PAVÉ LINK).
- 5: socket tags on the three flex cords (1 · LAG GAYA, 2 · 10% OFF · BUY2, 3 · 20% OFF · CODE BUY3).
- 6: fifteen-cup ring diagram.
- 7: outline traced from the piece.
- 8: RESERVED table tent.
- 9: fan-regulator dial (FLASH to GLOW).
- 10: all-on switchboard.

F2 CARD
- Bone on ink, on a 0-92% ink #1A1614 gradient rising 380 px from the bottom.
- White Naira wordmark 56 px; name in Jost 500 26 px .2em; price in Cormorant 56 px; the switchboard as its line; offer box in Jost 26 px with a 2 px bone border and a saffron diamond separator.
- Feed text stays inside x 72-1008, y 84-1266. Story text stays inside y 270-1250, with nothing under Meta's reply bar.
camps.brandFeatures:
- The white Naira wordmark heads the F2 card on every dark plate.
- The switchboard's ivory plate is bone #F4F0E8 and its neon indicators are saffron #E8A33A. Both are kit tokens, so the house palette is literally the switch. The seven-segment log is saffron too: the brand's accent is the colour of the inverter's display.
- Type is Velista, Cormorant italic and Jost only; the ₹ appears only in Cormorant. The log's digits are SVG segments, never a fourth font.
- Rooms are ink #1A1614 and cocoa #3B2620, with one accent per card: the piece's own colour.

camps.sellLever:
Wedding-season evenings are when she is seen and when the lights fail: dim shamianas, dead generators, ring lights that die before the photos. Each card sells one piece as the thing that still shines under one of the ten lights of a power cut, using that piece's real way with light (polish, pavé, separate stones in cups, a braid, satin). The joke is a product demonstration, and every slow piece gets a reason to be wanted tonight.

BUY3 LOGIC
- Every Indian home keeps backups for the power cut: the inverter, the candles, the maachis. Keep three pieces the same way, one each for the sangeet, the mehendi and the reception.
- Card 5, 'EK LAG GAYA. DO BAAKI.', puts the ladder in the picture: three bulb holders, one fitted with the pair, two still empty. Masking-tape tags on the cords read '1 · LAG GAYA', '2 · 10% OFF · BUY2', '3 · 20% OFF · CODE BUY3'. A pair is one piece, so the count is honest.
- Card 10, 'BIJLI AAYI.', flips every switch on; the last one is 'BUY3 · 20% OFF'.
- Every card's offer box carries BUY2 and BUY3.
- Every primary text says 'Any 3 pieces, 20% off with BUY3' before character 125.

PRODUCTS
- The Toggle (77 units) opens as the anchor.
- The pre-order pieces (Prism, Verdant Cushion, Rivière, Aqua Heart, Petite Square) say 'pre-order' and never promise dispatch.
- Recheck stock on launch day: the cards list Bold Nocturne and Rivière at 19 and the Marquise Coil Cuff at 10. No ad says 'last few' or 'limited'.

CAMPAIGN SLOTS
- OUTCOME: 1, 2, 8. PAIN: 4, 6. OBJECTION: 3, 7, 9. OFFER: 5, 10.
- Prospecting runs the four motivation sets.
- Retargeting runs TRUST (3, 7, 9) and SELL (4, 5, 6, 10).
- Reels: 1, 4, 10. Card 8's 'pandrah saal baad' is the cleanest single static for the 35-44 set and for gift-buying men 18-24.

Carousel: switch off 'show best-performing cards first' so the dark-to-light arc holds.
camps.carouselText: Bijli gayi. Chamak nahi. Any 3 pieces, 20% off with BUY3. Ten pieces under the ten lights of a power cut, from the maachis to the lalten, for the sangeet, the mehendi and the reception. Naira Petite. Chamak chalu.
camps.changes:
PUSHED (crazier and sharper; the world, product order, angles, layers, arc, F2 card and switchboard are kept):
1) THE BIG ONE: ten lights. Seven of the ten plates leaned on a candle (as key or fill), so the dark frames blurred into one 'piece by candlelight' look. Now every card has a different Indian power-cut light, named in the log: CHAANDNI, MAACHIS, TORCH, 200 PHONES, PADOSI KA SCOOTER, EMERGENCY LIGHT, LALTEN, MOMBATTI, DIYA, MAINS. Each light is a different test of the finish, so the demonstration is ten tests rather than one. Only card 8 is lit by a candle; card 9's candles have burnt out.
2) THE LOG is now a saffron seven-segment SVG readout, like the inverter's display, plus 'ROSHNI: <light>'. It dims on card 9 and turns ink on card 10. The power cut reads at a glance before the headline does.
3) Lit type is readable at 200 px: the mask floor rises from 20% to 55%. Card 3 gets a hard torch-circle mask that cuts through the headline, and card 4 a dead/lit two-tone headline.
4) Card 1: fixed the logic, since there is no candle at 8:41 when nobody has found the maachis. The only light is moonlight through the window grille, plus a warm kicker that keeps the clasp the one warm thing. The strands now run straight down the wall like the house's surface wiring. The Reel no longer brings the lights back (no inverter beep or bright grade at the end), so the payoff is saved for card 10; a cloud crossing the moon is the new motion.
5) Card 2: new beat 'mil gayi. aur andar rang tha'. The '?' dot is a burnt match head. A fresh strike streak is added to the box.
6) Card 3: the torch now proves something. It passes through the stone and drops a pool of clean green light on the silk (a clear stone throws its colour), with a leader that is printed only if the plate shows it. The fireflies are replaced by a sunburst of round dots, the halo's own shape. New beat 'hara hi rahega'.
7) Card 4: the pain gets its answer in the same frame. She is mid bhangra 'bulb' step, the hand cupped overhead and the pavé link where the bulb would be. The headline becomes 'GENERATOR GAYA. / BULB LAGAO.' (dead line, lit line). In the Reel the dholi plays on unplugged; this is the camp's dhol card. Field of view goes to 12 cm for the raised hand.
8) Card 5: the offer is now a chore every Indian has done in the dark: 'EK LAG GAYA. DO BAAKI.' There are three bulb holders; the pair hangs from the first (one hoop in each bayonet slot) and two hang empty. Masking-tape tags on the cords (1 · LAG GAYA, 2 · 10% OFF, 3 · 20% OFF · CODE BUY3) replace the separate inverter meter, so the picture is the BUY3 ladder. A pair is one piece, so the count stays honest. The light is a neighbour's scooter headlight through the stair window.
9) Card 6: the emergency lamp's flat cool light replaces the candle. New beat 'ek ghante mein photos'. Kept otherwise; it was already the camp's strongest geometry.
10) Card 7: lalten light (exact for the 35-44 buyer, who played this game by kerosene light). The shadow swan wears a ridged collar where the cuff sits, with a 'HANS NE BHI PEHNA' label printed only if it shows.
11) Card 8: the outcome is sharper and aimed at the core buyer: 'PANDRAH SAAL BAAD, / CANDLELIGHT DINNER.' It is the first candlelight dinner in fifteen years, on dal-chawal and steel thalis. The frame is now a tilted lean-in, so it no longer repeats card 10's upright ear frame.
12) Card 9: the story now holds. Forty-five minutes in, the candles have burnt down and gone out, and a diya off-frame is the last light. New beat 'sasta nahi, satin hai' answers the ₹699 doubt.
13) Card 10: card 1's porcelain switch sits soft on the doorframe, now on, to close the loop. The Reel opens on diya light and the log turns ink.
14) Every prompt now asks for the subject centred and sized as a share of the frame height (the 19 Nov ruling), instead of percentage positions.

ads.picture: 8:41 PM, the first second of the cut, before anyone has found the maachis, so there is no candle yet. The only light is the moon through an old iron window grille: a soft, cool lattice across one side of a limewashed drawing-room wall. On that wall is a vintage round ivory porcelain toggle switch, 45 mm across. The Toggle Link Chain hangs from its lever by its own sailor ring, with the stone-set bar threaded through the ring and facing us. Its two paperclip strands drop straight down the wall side by side, like the twin flex of old surface wiring leaving the switch: the chain has become the house's wiring. One small warm kicker catches the ring. In a cool, blue-grey room the clasp is the only warm thing, and the brightest. It stops the thumb because it is the pun made physical, the toggle literally on the switch in the dark, and because the chain is quietly doing the job of the electrics.
ads.prompt: Witty cinematic advertising photograph, vertical 9:16, eye level, a close still life on a wall at night. Reference 1 is the authority on this exact necklace; reference 2 on its clasp. Preserve it exactly: a 50 cm chain, 4 mm wide, of elongated paperclip links (about 4 x 11 mm) in polished 18k gold tone; 1 thick round spring-gate sailor ring about 22 mm across (about 14 mm opening, small push-pin nub, ribbed gate collar) and 1 short straight bar about 15 mm long set with 1 row of about 9 tiny clear stones, on a jump ring. No pendant, no other stones. It must stay a sailor ring with a straight bar 0.6-0.7x the ring, never a plain donut ring, a lobster clasp, or a curved or multi-row pave bar. ads.risk: The satin may render mirror-polished or pale silver, the hoops may melt into or merge with the wax, and a flame may creep back into the frame. Burnt-down stubs in wide pools may also push the hoops off level. Hedge take: the pair standing in a cooled pool of wax on the steel plate beside one snuffed stub, same light.
ads.why10: The jury said satin dies in the dark. This card makes satin the soft light itself and teaches the finish in one surreal swap, and the story now holds: forty-five minutes in, the candles have burnt down and only the diya is left. 'Sasta nahi, satin hai' answers the ₹699 doubt in four words, then the 14 mm truth and three tagged claims back it up. The dimmed headline makes 'dheemi' something you see.

ads.variant: Default Title, 18k gold tone (refs 02.jpg pair packshot, 01.jpg construction macro; never 03.jpg for scale)
ads.picture: 9:31 PM: the inverter beeps and the lights come back. This is the only lit card in the camp. We see her from behind her shoulder as she steps through a doorway into a warm, suddenly bright drawing room: the bulbs glow soft and the fan is just starting to turn. By the doorframe, soft and out of focus, is the same small round porcelain switch from card 1, now on. Her low bun, her nape and one ear show the Petite Square hoop snug under the lobe: square outside, round inside, with two pinhead pearls peeking at the side. It stops the thumb after nine dark cards because the screen literally lights up, and the double meaning lands: the bijli that came back is her.
ads.prompt: Warm cinematic on-body advertising photograph, vertical 9:16, shot from behind her left shoulder as she steps through a doorway. Reference 1 is the authority on this exact hoop; reference 2 is the authority on its construction. Preserve it exactly, 0 stones: 1 chunky tube bent into a 15 mm square, 4 softly rounded corners, round opening inside; 1 thin snap wire across the top; 1 hinge seam on the bottom bar; 4 white 1.5 mm pearls on the outer side walls, 2 per side. Mirror-polished 18k gold tone. It must stay 4 pinhead pearls on the side walls, never more, bigger or on the front face; square outside, round inside, never a round hoop, never a hard-cornered box. Do not redesign or add anything. THE CROP: the back of her head and nape, dark hair in a low bun, one ear from behind with the hoop worn snug under the lower lobe, legs vertical, hinge at the bottom, the snap wire through the lobe, the pearls facing sideways; the head turned away, the frame edge just behind the jaw hinge: no cheek, eye, lashes, nose or lips anywhere. A young Indian woman, light wheatish skin with warm honey undertones, natural texture and fine downy hair at the nape; a soft ivory silk collar at the bottom. THE WORLD: the second the power comes back. She stands in a doorway; the drawing room ahead has just lit up: warm bulbs glowing small and soft in deep focus blur, a ceiling fan just starting to turn as a gentle blur, limewashed walls in warm light. On the doorframe beside her, far out of focus, one small round ivory porcelain switch. SCALE: the hoop is 15 mm, about a quarter of the ear's height, a little smaller than a 1 rupee coin; each pearl a pinhead; the snap wire disappears into the lobe with a soft contact shadow. LIGHT: warm bright evening interior light from the room ahead as the soft key, rimming the ear; one small hard specular kicker from the upper right gives the polished tube a crisp bright edge and each pearl a tiny round catchlight. The hoop is the most saturated thing in the frame. COMPOSITION: the ear and hoop centred, a little right, the ear about a quarter of the frame height; calm warm out-of-focus room above for a headline; calm hair, nape and collar below. Field of view about 8 cm wide at the ear. Shallow depth of field, the hoop needle-sharp. Natural film grain, warm Indian evening, editorial jewellery campaign. No plastic skin. No four-point star glints. No text, letters, numbers, logos or markings. No face, no profile, no mirror, no second earring. One product only.

ads.motion:
Kling 3.0, 5 s from the lit plate.
- What moves: the ceiling fan in the room ahead spins up from still to a soft blur; a few loose hairs at the nape lift in the new breeze; the bulbs bloom gently; the camera makes a slow 3% pull-back.
- What never moves: the ear, the hoop, the bun.

Edit:
- Open on the same plate graded near black, with one warm diya glow on the hoop (the end of the power cut).
- 0.6 s: a tubelight starter ticks and flickers three times.
- 1 s: the inverter beeps, the full lit grade snaps on, and a family cheers 'aa gayi!' off-screen.
- 'BIJLI AAYI.' switches on letter by letter, like bulbs, and the seven-segment clock turns from saffron to ink.
- 3 s: the beat lands and the four pearl circles pop in one by one.

ads.risk: The pearl count and size may drift (models add a fifth pearl or move them onto the front face), the hoop may render at 1.5x, and a cheek may leak at the frame edge. The background switch may grow too large or sharp; it must stay a soft, small shape. Hedge take: a macro of the hoop hung on the same porcelain switch as card 1, now in warm lit-room light (the bookend), field of view 6 cm.
ads.why10: After nine dark cards the carousel ends with the lights on. 'BIJLI AAYI.' lands both meanings at once: the power is back and the stunner walked in. 'Chaar chaand' makes the four pearls both the joke and the proof. The all-on switchboard turns BUY3 into the last switch she flips, and the card 1 switch on the doorframe closes the loop for anyone who swiped all ten.

camps.name: EK MATRA KI KAMI.
camps.idea:
WORLD. This December the most-read Hindi in her house is on the fridge: the shaadi card. Every ad is one blank invitation for one function: roka, mehendi, sangeet, ring ceremony, reception, every function, cocktail night, winter shaadi, haldi, and the programme page. Each is shot as a still life on that function's own ground (silk, velvet, satin, knit, banana leaf, water). On every card a Devanagari word is one mark short. The real Naira piece lies, stands or is pinned exactly where that mark goes, and HTML sets the rest of the word around it. The jewel does not sit next to the word. It is part of it. Absolut ran a long series on one rule, that the bottle is the shape in the scene; this camp's rule is that the jewel is the mark in the word, so ten different pictures read as one campaign at thumb speed.

THE DEVICE: EVERY MARK IN THE SCRIPT IS CAST BY A REAL PIECE. A chain is the shirorekha, the top bar Hindi writers draw last, the stroke that turns separate letters into one word (Toggle on पक्का, Bold Nocturne on तीनों). Two green studs are chandrabindus, a dot over a bowl, which is exactly what the Verdant Circlet is (मेहँदी? हाँ). A five-stone smiling arc is the moon over पाँच, five. A ring is the anusvara of अंगूठी, and a bangle is the anusvara of कंगन. A choker's drop is the ा that turns हर (every) into हार (necklace). A solitaire is the bindu (the word means both dot and drop) of बूँद, drop. A pair of hoops are the mirror curls ि and ी of किसी, and the two ी of पीली.

NEW: EACH FUNCTION WRITES IN ITS OWN INK. The word is no longer always foil. Each function's own material writes it. Roka: gold foil. Mehendi: henna paste, piped from the cone that lies on the card, with its tip where the word ends. Sangeet: lilac-silver foil. Ring ceremony: one giant silver-foil letter. Reception: gold foil under cold-spark light. Every function: gold foil on the stack. Cocktail night: a frosted etch in an acrylic card under a film of water. Winter shaadi: gold foil. Haldi: turmeric paste, finger-painted by the turmeric-coated hand in the picture, whose fingertip rests where the last stroke ends. Programme page: gold foil. The device stays the same and the texture changes ten times, so the run never reads as one card shown ten times. On cards 2 and 9 the writer is in the frame: the cone and the finger.

NEW: THE TEACHER'S RED PEN. The insight is a school memory, so the school's mark appears. On the minimal-pair cards (2 हा/हाँ, 4 अगूठी/अंगूठी, 6 हर/हार) the wrong word is printed small and struck through in terracotta red-pen ink, and a hand-drawn caret points up into the jewel that fixes it. Every Indian who lost half a mark knows the gesture before they can read the word, which makes the joke work for non-Hindi readers too.

SCALE LAW: THE TYPE OWNS THE SCALE. Each piece is shot at its real size and closer than before (8.3-18 px per mm on the 1080 frame). The foil word is then set so that the missing mark's natural size equals the jewel, even when that makes the word giant and runs it off the card and the frame. The piece never shrinks to fit the word, so stand-alone pieces fill 17-46% of the frame width, and the two chains and the bracelet cross it entirely. No plate reaches 19 px per mm, so no 'shown magnified' tag is needed; every size line states the listed mm. The two-script gloss restates the whole word, small and complete, for anyone the crop leaves behind. Generated pieces drift toward the centre, so the prompts give placement in words and the type is set to the plate after generation: the word follows the jewel, never the other way round.

HOW LISTING FACTS APPEAR. Never as a badge. They come out of the card in three places: the micro-label on the dashed ring (the mark's real Devanagari name and the true size), sense 2 of the dictionary gloss, and the F2 card's one line. The proofs are now physical, inside the picture. Card 4: the dashed ring turns into a ring gauge (US 5-9) round the open back, and a snipped measuring thread lies retired on the velvet. Card 7: the whole acrylic card sits under a film of water, a fresh drop rings out beside the stone, and a bead of water sits on top of it. Card 9: water beads on the braid while the hand that wrote the word is still coated in turmeric.

TEN FUNCTIONS, TEN SHOTS. 1 roka: Toggle as the bar of पक्का, top-down with fingertips (animated: the loose letters snap up under the chain). 2 mehendi: Verdant Circlet as the two moons of मेहँदी? हाँ, piped in henna from the cone in frame (animated, HTML only). 3 sangeet: Prism pinned through an upright plum card like a jeweller's earring card, five paper dress-code tabs along its top edge, three of them matched to the stones. 4 ring ceremony: Verdant band standing in a velvet ring tray as the dot of a giant अ, with the ring gauge and the retired thread. 5 reception: Bold Nocturne under a far curtain of cold sparks as the bar of तीनों (animated). 6 every function: Marquise choker on a stepped stack of function cards, shot at a steep angle, the ा of हार. 7 cocktail night: Serpentine Silver on a wet acrylic invitation, the bindu of बूँद, the dashed ring as a real ripple (animated). 8 winter shaadi: Torsade standing like pop-up type on oxblood with cable knit behind, the ि and ी of किसी, with a kaala teeka for the aunties. 9 haldi: Woven hoops written into पीली by a turmeric fingertip on a banana leaf. 10 programme page: Molten bangle standing like a monument, the dot of कंगन, under सपरिवार पधारें and the offer ladder (animated). Cards 1-5 run first, 6-10 second.

RULES THAT DO NOT BEND. Every glyph is HTML. The generated card is blank: no monograms, deity marks, kalash, Om, Ganesha, henna designs or pseudo-script, and any take with letter-like marks is rejected. No faces and no eyes; the two hands are bare. One product per picture; thread, cone, katori, easel and sparks are props. Copy follows each product card's use and avoid lists: green cubic zirconia, never emerald; shell pearl; 18k gold tone and rhodium silver tone; no claims on Prism, Torsade or Molten; no water near the Toggle; the listing word 'huggies' is never printed, so the F2 reads TORSADE HOOPS. The pre-order pieces (Prism, Torsade, Molten) never promise arrival before a function: their urgency says 'this season'.
camps.insight: Every Indian who learned Hindi lost marks for one missing matra, under a red-pen caret, and every Hindi teacher said the same line: एक मात्रा की ग़लती से अर्थ का अनर्थ हो जाता है (one wrong mark turns meaning into nonsense). A matra is the smallest thing on the page and it changes everything, which is exactly what a ₹699-1,899 piece does to an outfit she already owns. In a 35-44 woman's house this December, the most-read Hindi is the shaadi card on the fridge, and its functions are why she needs something new by a date. So the season's own object carries a word that is one mark short, and her slow piece is that mark: without it the word is wrong; with it the word, and the look, is complete. Hindi readers get it in a beat and feel clever. Everyone else gets a jewel still life, the red-pen correction they remember from school, a Roman headline in Hinglish, and a two-script gloss that tells the joke twice.
camps.textualGraphic:
Six type layers, locked to each other by the jewel.
1. THE WORD, IN THE FUNCTION'S INK (SVG over the plate). Rozha One for display Devanagari and Tiro Devanagari Hindi for small Devanagari (both added from Google Fonts, for Devanagari only; set arrows and ticks in SVG, because Rozha has no arrow glyph). Glyphs become outlines, and the outlines are filled with one of four ink recipes. FOIL (cards 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10): gold-light #E4C889 → deep gold #B8913F → #E4C889 at 100°, or bone #F4F0E8 → #A8A39A on the rhodium pieces; a 1 px emboss aimed at the plate's key light (a 1 px #FFF6DC highlight at 45% top-left and a 1 px ink line at 30% bottom-right); a 6% paper-grain overlay so it reads as stamped, not pasted. HENNA (card 2): the Rozha outlines used as a skeleton and piped as a 9-14 px stroke in henna brown #5A2E14, with a 1.5 px raised highlight #B97A4A top-left, a 0.6 px dried-crack noise and rounded blob ends. FROST ETCH (card 7): bone at 72% with 2 px frost noise and a 1 px inner glow, no emboss, so it reads as sandblasted into acrylic; a 0.8 px refraction offset under the water film. TURMERIC (card 9): brush strokes in #E8A33A with 2 px #B8730A dried edges, a soft impasto highlight and a fingerprint-whorl texture where each stroke starts and stops; the last stroke ends on the plate's own fingertip smudge. CSS matrix3d puts the word on the card's plane in the angled plates (cards 4, 6, 8, 10). Scale law: the missing mark's natural size equals the jewel's real size, so the word may be giant and cropped.
2. THE GHOST STROKE. The missing mark itself is printed as a blind deboss (paper-colour fill, 1 px inner shadow, no ink) exactly under the jewel, so its outline peeks round the piece: a non-reader sees that the shapes match, and a reader sees the impression the jewel is resting in.
3. THE MATRA RING. A 1.5 px dashed gold-light circle (dash 6, gap 5; an ellipse in perspective; bone on the rhodium cards) hugs the jewel at +18 px. A 1 px leader runs to a Jost 22 px caps micro-label, tracked .14em, that opens with the mark's own name in Tiro Devanagari 24 px: शिरोरेखा · SHIROREKHA · 50 CM; चंद्रबिंदु × 2 · CHANDRABINDU · 16.8 MM; अनुस्वार · ANUSVARA; आ की मात्रा · AA MATRA; बिंदु · BINDU · 10 MM; इ की मात्रा · ई की मात्रा · 20 MM EACH. Two cards transform it. On card 4 it becomes a RING GAUGE: five foil ticks along the open back, labelled US 5 · 6 · 7 · 8 · 9 in Jost 18 px. On card 7 it becomes the RIPPLE: three concentric dashed rings registered to the real ripple in the plate. On TRUST cards the ring sprouts kit callouts (Jost caps over a Jost line, with a 2 px leader ending in an open circle on metal, never on a stone).
4. THE TEACHER'S CARET (new). A hand-drawn ‸ in a 3 px terracotta #B5502F red-pen stroke, with a small ink pool at the turn, points up into the jewel. The wrong word sits beside it, struck through in the same pen. It is used only on the minimal-pair cards (2, 4, 6) and only on ivory paper, so it always reads as red ink.
5. THE VELISTA HEADLINE. The Hinglish line in Roman caps: 108-124 px on Story and 88-100 px on Feed, bone on the ground (ink where it falls on ivory paper), at most two lines, with no digits, dashes or ₹. A question headline may set its answer line in gold-light (card 5: TEENON CHAHIYE? / TEENON LO.).
6. THE TWO-SCRIPT GLOSS. Under the word sits a dictionary entry in the manner of an old Hindustani-English dictionary (the style only; no publication is named). It gives the headword in Tiro Devanagari 40 px, the Jost 22 px phonetic and part of speech ('/pak·kaa/ adj.'), and then numbered senses in Cormorant Garamond italic 34-38 px: sense 1 is the word, and sense 2 is the piece with its listing truths. The minimal-pair cards add one Jost caps line, WITHOUT · हा · A SIGH   WITH · हाँ · YES, with the red-pen strike on the wrong word.
Then the F2 card. Prices are set only in Cormorant from the ₹ subset. On Feed, the card's foot line reads RSVP · NAIRAFLORE.COM in Jost 20 px caps. Safe areas come from the kit: Feed text x 72-1008, y 84-1266; Story text y 270-1250. Plates are generated at 9:16, with the jewel and its type zone inside the central 4:5 window (Feed = Story y 285-1635, or any 4:5 window chosen per RULINGS §4).
MOTION (cards 1, 2, 5, 7, 10). Each animated card performs the meaning of its own mark. On 1 the loose letters snap up under the chain. On 2 the henna pipes itself to the cone's tip. On 5 the answer line stamps in like a wax seal. On 7 the dashed rings ride the real ripple. On 10 the programme ticks in. Kling 3.0 (5 s, locked camera) moves only the world and the light, and the piece stays rigid. Card 2 is HTML-only, so no video model ever touches the studs' construction. The Feed static is the end frame.
camps.brandFeatures: The Naira wordmark is the invitation's seal: 56 px inside a hairline circle at the card's top right, set on the card's plane where a couple's monogram would be. It is gold-light foil on the gold cards, bone on the rhodium cards, frosted on the acrylic card 7, and gold foil even on the henna and turmeric cards, so the brand mark stays constant while the ink changes. It is the only 'printed' brand on the card, and it makes every invitation unmistakably a Naira one at thumb speed. The F2 card sits under the gloss in the kit lockup. On Feed it is the full block: wordmark, name in Jost 26 px caps .2em, Cormorant 56 px price, one Jost 26 px line, and the offer box with the gold-light diamond separator. On Story it compacts to name · price, line and offer box inside y 1085-1250, because the seal already carries the wordmark. The listing word 'huggies' is never set in type, so card 8's F2 name reads TORSADE HOOPS. Each function owns one palette token as its ground. Velista, Cormorant and Jost stay the only Latin faces; Rozha One and Tiro Devanagari Hindi are added for Devanagari only. The camp owns three marks, drawn at the same weight on every ad: the dashed gold ring, the ghost stroke, and the terracotta red-pen caret on the minimal-pair cards. Shipping line: concept-50 RULINGS §6 records the owner asking for FREE INSURED SHIPPING · CASH ON DELIVERY on every ad, but this step's hard rules say never free shipping, and on 20 Nov the store still charged ₹150 below ₹3,000, so it is left off. If the owner confirms and the checkout matches, it takes the F2 foot line (Jost 20 px caps, after RSVP · NAIRAFLORE.COM) on every card.
camps.palette: Each function has its own ground, matched by a kit token in the HTML. Roka: oxblood #6E1F23 silk with an ivory card. Mehendi: sage-deep #5E7A6C silk, ivory card, henna-brown #5A2E14 type. Sangeet: a plum #4A2540 card, lilac foil, and five muted paper tabs (turmeric, leaf green, lilac, rose, ivory). Ring ceremony: a coral-deep #C8664A velvet tray, an ivory card and silver foil. Reception: a cocoa #3B2620 card on black-brown satin under a far, dim curtain of warm cold-sparks. Every function: an ivory top card on ink #1A1614 silk, with the stack's edges stepping out in sage, saffron, plum and oxblood. Cocktail night: smoked ink-blue acrylic under a water film, on peacock teal (the silver piece's best ground), frost-white type. Winter shaadi: an oxblood card on bone #F4F0E8 cable knit. Haldi: an ivory card on banana-leaf green with marigold, and turmeric #E8A33A type with #B8730A edges. Programme page: ivory on terracotta #B5502F silk. Type colours: headlines bone #F4F0E8 (ink #1A1614 on paper), foil and beats gold-light #E4C889, labels bone at 85%; the rhodium cards switch the foil to bone→silver, and the red pen is terracotta #B5502F on ivory only. The piece is always the most saturated or brightest thing in its frame: green on ivory, pastel on plum, silver on ink, teal and coral, gold on dark or ivory, never gold on saffron. The pave link must outshine every spark on card 5.
camps.sellLever: The lever is occasion plus completion. Each card is a function she attends this season, so each slow piece becomes the named answer to 'what do I wear to the mehendi?'. The mark it completes makes it feel necessary rather than optional: without it, the word is wrong, and the red pen says so. BUY3 logic: functions come in threes (mehendi, sangeet, shaadi), so the offer line on most cards is TEEN FUNCTION, TEEN MATRA · BUY3 · 20% OFF. Card 5 sets the offer as a dialogue at the counter: her question, TEENON CHAHIYE?, and our answer, TEENON LO., with the shopkeeper's 'hum kam laga denge' in the primary text, so the code reads as the haggle she has already won. Card 6 escalates to BUY4 at 30% ('a new haar for every function'). Card 10 turns the wedding card's own idiom into the ladder: सपरिवार पधारें, 'please come with the family', means bring the bangle's family (two pieces 10%, three 20%, four 30%). Retargeting runs the self-completing trio carousel (हार, अंगूठी, कंगन: Marquise Drop Choker ₹999, Verdant Eternity Band ₹1,049, Molten Panel Bangle ₹999) to a BUY3 collection, and the Toggle Link Chain (77 units, ₹999) is the named anchor every BUY3 landing page leads with. Prospecting sets: PAIN 3, 6, 9; OUTCOME 1, 2, 8; OBJECTION 4, 7; OFFER 5, 10. There is no fake urgency, no compare-at or struck prices and no invented 'last few' counts. Pre-order pieces say 'this season', never 'in time for'.

camps.changes:
PUSHED against the k08 bible above. The world, the device, the product order, the angles and layers, the scale law and the F2 card are kept.
(1) TEN INKS. Nine of ten words were gold or silver foil, so the run read as one card ten times. Now each function writes in its own material: henna paste on the mehendi card, a frosted etch in acrylic on cocktail night, turmeric paste on haldi, and foil elsewhere. On cards 2 and 9 the writer is in the frame: the cone's tip and the turmeric fingertip sit where the word ends.
(2) THE TEACHER'S RED PEN (new layer). The insight is a school memory, so the school's mark is now drawn: a terracotta caret inserts the jewel and the wrong word is struck through on cards 2 (हा/हाँ), 4 (अगूठी/अंगूठी, new) and 6 (हर/हार). Non-Hindi readers get the correction gesture at a glance.
(3) Crazier proofs, inside the picture. Card 4: the matra ring becomes a US 5-9 ring gauge round the open back, and a snipped measuring thread lies on the velvet labelled THE THREAD TRICK · RETIRED (every Indian ring-size mission). Card 7: the whole invitation is now smoked acrylic under a water film, with a fresh drop ringing out beside the stone; the dashed matra ring becomes the real ripple, and the Reel rides it. Card 9: the turmeric-coated hand wrote पीली, and the hoops beside it carry water beads and no stain.
(4) Card 1 motion performs the shirorekha: the letters start loose and crooked and snap up under the chain one by one, so letters become a word when the line joins them, as two families become one at a roka.

Reference 1 is the authority on this exact piece, standing as it stands there; reference 2 shows its true size worn.
