camps.name: AAJ KA BHAAV.
camps.insight: In the 2026 wedding season the per-gram rate is the loudest number in every Indian family. It is forwarded to the family group each morning, it decides how many of the five functions she can dress for, and the board at the jeweller only ever goes up. She has been trained to ask 'bhaav kya hai?' and to distrust a price that moves. Naira cannot and should not compete on metal; it competes on certainty. A rate board whose number never changes turns 'by the piece, not by the gram' into relief. THOK BHAAV, the wholesale rate every mother already uses at the mandi, turns BUY3 into a bargain she knows how to take, and PALDA BARABAR KARO turns it into a physical instruction. The season gives the camp its other two rituals: the blouse 'naap' she gives the darzi (so a ring size is a measurement she already understands) and the five-function marathon that her earlobes have to survive. BHAAV also means three things: the rate, an attitude ('bhaav khaana', acting pricey) and a feeling. That gives each piece a personality line: BHAAV NAHI KHAATI (the ring that doesn't act pricey), SAADA BHAAV, NA BHAARI NA BHAAV.
camps.textualGraphic:
THE BHAAV BOARD: Naira's own dot-matrix rate board, built in SVG over the picture, plus one honest instrument per card, registered to the picture.

1) THE BOARD
- Panel: ink #1A1614 in a 12 px brushed-aluminium frame (linear-gradient 100deg #DAD5CC, #8E8982, #EFEAE2, #9A958D), with a 1 px ink keyline and four 8 px slotted screw heads.
- Glyphs: real Jost 600 caps and tabular figures (₹ from the kit's Noto subset), set as SVG text and painted only through a mask of round dots, so every character is made of whole dots.
- Sizes: the hero board uses 6 px dots on an 8 px pitch with a 64 px cap height. The ticker strip uses 4 px dots on a 5 px pitch with a 30 px cap height.
- Lit dots: a radial gradient from a saffron #E8A33A core to a coral-deep #C8664A rim, plus a 3 px feGaussianBlur glow merged at 55%.
- Unlit dots: the whole grid in oxblood #6E1F23 at 15%, so the panel reads as a real board between the letters.
- Rows: 'AAJ' with the price right-aligned; 'KAL' with the same price; a chrome rule (1 px gold-light at 40% over 1 px ink); then the offer row. The offer row is the only one lit in gold-light #E4C889 dots: 'THOK BHAAV · BUY3 · 20% OFF'.
- Units are the shop's own: '/JODI' for a pair, '/PIECE' for one piece.
- The hero board runs on cards 1, 4 (at the foot) and 8. On the other seven it shrinks to a one-row ticker, so the instrument and the piece lead.
- OVERFLOW (card 4 only): the LOOK row has no number. Its lit dots march right as a solid run at full cap height, through the price field and past the aluminium frame, and the last 40-60 px of dots spill onto the picture and fade (glow only, no panel behind them). The board breaks because it cannot hold the look; the BHAAV row under it stays neat.

2) SHUTTER (card 1 motion only)
- An SVG rolling shutter in brushed galvanised grey: horizontal ribs at a 22 px pitch, each a 1 px highlight over a 2 px shadow, a slight sag at the bottom bar, two plain padlock hasps. No text, no graffiti, no shop name.
- It covers the full frame at 0 s and rolls up into a 40 px drum at the top edge in 0.6 s (ease-in, then a 6 px bounce), with a rattle. The drum fades as the fascia appears.

3) HEADLINE
- Velista caps in bone #F4F0E8, 84-96 px over two lines, up to 150 px for a one-word line, letter-spacing .02em, ligatures off. The second beat of a two-beat headline is gold-light.
- Beat: Cormorant Garamond italic 500, 40-44 px, gold-light, lower case. It carries the ₹ and the digits that Velista cannot.
- Type sits on velvet, darkness, hair or petals, never on the piece.

4) INSTRUMENTS (one per card)
- SCALE LCD: a die-cut SVG display, ink glass with a 2 px chrome bezel. Seven-segment digits in pista #B9C98A, unlit segments at 12%. Caption in Jost 18 px caps: 'LISTED WEIGHT · BY THE PIECE, NOT BY THE GRAM'. Listed grams only.
- CONE TICKS: three hairline gold-light ticks registered to the rendered cone at the heights whose rendered diameter matches each size. If they fall closer than 40 px apart, they fan out on 1 px leaders to labels spaced 64 px apart. Labels in Jost 24 px caps: 'US 8 · 18.1 MM', 'US 7 · 17.3 MM', 'US 6 · 16.5 MM', with a caption in Jost 16 px caps: 'INSIDE DIAMETER'. The US 7 tick, where the ring sits, carries a gold-light diamond.
- TAG STRINGS: fig callouts drawn as a jeweller's tag thread. A 1.5 px bone line ends in a 10 px open circle that lands on metal, never on a stone. Label in Jost 22 px caps over Cormorant italic 28 px.
- GHOST SLOTS: dashed gold-light circles (3 px, dash 10/8) the size of the piece, each with '+ one' in Cormorant italic.
- PARCHI: a die-cut estimate slip torn from the pad in the picture. Bone, zig-zag perforated top, sky #9EC3D6 ruled lines on a 38 px pitch, entries in plum #4A2540 Cormorant italic 32 px, a printed header in Jost 18 px caps. Rotated −3° with a 12 px soft shadow.
- STRING TAG: a bone dumbbell tag on a thread looped round an earring post.
- RING-ZERO: Jost 500 numerals sized to the real sailor ring, so the ring reads as the 0 of '20%'.

5) COUNTER STRIP (the F2 card, compressed)
- Name in Jost 24 px caps, tracked .2em.
- Price in Cormorant 56 px.
- One listing line in Jost 24 px.
- Offer box: kit .offer with the gold-light diamond separator.
- Footer in Jost 20 px.

6) LOCK
- The piece is first: 40-55% of the width and the loudest colour.
- Text stays under 30% of the frame.
- Feed 4:5 is the 9:16 frame cropped from y 90, so the piece extent sits at Feed y 380-910 and Story y 470-1000.
- Story text stays within y 270-1250.
- 'SHOWN MAGNIFIED' is printed only at 19 or more Feed px per listed mm (cards 1, 3 and 9). Every other card prints its listed size plainly.
camps.brandFeatures:
- Fascia: the Naira wordmark is the shop's fascia, in gold-light #E4C889, 56 px, centred at the top over a 1 px gold-light hairline (x 400-680), as the sign above the rate board. In Story it moves into the board frame's top bar at 32 px. On card 1's clip it appears as the shutter drum fades, the way a sign lights after the shutter goes up.
- F2 card: compressed into a 'counter strip' at the foot. Product name in Jost 24 px caps, price in Cormorant Garamond 56 px, one listing line in Jost 24 px, and the offer box (kit .offer) with its gold-light diamond separator.
- Type: Velista caps for every headline (bone, key word gold-light), Cormorant italic for beats and prices, Jost for every label. The LED glyphs are Jost too, so even the rate board speaks in the house face.
- Palette tokens only, and the piece is always the loudest colour.
- Footer: 'CASH ON DELIVERY · PAY AT THE DOOR' (truth check: the RULINGS §6 'FREE INSURED SHIPPING' line is held off; see changes). COD line in the copy: 'pay at the door, not at the counter'.
- Sign-off on the carousel and the last card: 'Naira Petite. Kal bhi yahi.'
camps.sellLever:
Certainty plus quantity.

THE HOOK is relief: a price that holds while everything else in the season climbs (metal, flowers, the weight of what she wears for five functions).

THE CLOSE is THOK BHAAV = BUY3, 20% off any three, with BUY4 at 30% off printed only after the owner's margin check.
- Every board and ticker carries the offer.
- Three cards make three pieces visible while showing one product:
  - card 2: the sailor ring is the 0 of '20%';
  - card 5: the empty pan holds two ghost slots, and only BUY3 balances the scale;
  - card 10: the torn estimate slip has blank lines 'didi ke liye' and 'apne liye'.

| Brushed ₹699 + Toggle ₹999 + Woven ₹1,049 | ₹2,747 | ₹2,198 | ₹440 a purchase |

Today's single-piece order is about ₹1,150, so a BUY3 basket roughly doubles the order value. That is the realistic route from ROAS 2.2 to 5.

FORMAT: run it as a 10-card carousel, because catalogue-like choice is this account's ROAS engine. Each card links to its product; cards 5 and 10 link to a BUY3 collection. Card 1's clip runs as the Reels and Stories lead, and the carousel runs in Feed.

camps.changes:
WHAT I PUSHED (k09 v2, the 'make it crazier' pass)

Kept: the camp's core (the rate board that never moves, THOK BHAAV = BUY3, the BHAAV puns), the headlines on cards 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8 and 10, every card's angle and layer, and every claim gate.

1. Card 1 (PAIN, animated): the clip now opens the way every Indian shop opens.
   - An HTML rolling shutter rattles up, then the tube light ticks on twice.
   - The board's price fields roll upward like a live rate update, then clunk back onto exactly ₹699. No other number ever holds on screen, so it can never read as a compare-at price.
   - The marquee adds the comic third beat, PARSON KA BHAAV.
   - The pair grows from 40% to about half the frame width (field of view 6 cm → 5 cm), so 'Shown magnified' is now honest at about 22 px/mm.
2. Card 2 (OFFER): the beat goes from 'the wholesale rate, for three. four? 30%.' to 'the mandi rule, now at the jeweller's.', so the offer borrows a bargain she already wins every week. For Reels, the '2' flips to '3' to make '30%' for BUY4, used only after the margin check.
3. Card 3 (OUTCOME): the safe is now shot from inside, looking out as the door swings open a hand's width. One blade of cool shop light comes through the gap and lands on the ring alone, so 'out of the family locker' becomes a lighting event. New beat: 'the family-locker look, without the attitude: ₹1,049.'
4. Card 4 (OUTCOME/EDUCATION):
   - The stud was 1/8 of the frame (about 25 px on the 200 px sheet); the crop is now tighter, at about 1/6.
   - The headline moves onto the calm black hair at the top, and the hero board moves to the foot.
   - The board's LOOK row no longer blinks: its lit dots overflow the aluminium frame and spill onto the picture, because the board cannot hold what the look is worth. The BHAAV row stays neat at ₹1,099.
5. Card 5 (OFFER): the headline is now PALDA BARABAR KARO. ('even out the scale'), an instruction that is the offer. The hoops sink one pan, two ghost slots wait in the other, and only BUY3 balances it. 'By the piece, never by the gram' moves to the beat and primary text.
6. Card 6 (OBJECTION): the chain now lies in the scale pan beaded with shower droplets (never on the stone). One frame answers both objections: substance (the listed 10 g on the LCD) and daily wear (waterproof, which its tags allow).
7. Card 7 (OBJECTION):
   - Sibling camp k06 already lays a ring on a diagonal mandrel, so the instrument is now an upright steel sizing cone shot low like a column, its ridges reading as vertical flutes.
   - Three ticks carry each size's standard inside diameter: US 6 is 16.5 mm, US 7 is 17.3 mm and US 8 is 18.1 mm.
   - New beat: 'blouse ka naap diya? ring ka bhi do.' The darzi's wedding-season ritual answers the ring-size objection.
8. Card 8 (PAIN): the beat is sharpened to 'five flowers. one rate all season: ₹799.' The marigold pan and the phool-mandi board stay, because they are the carousel's colour break.
9. Card 9 (PAIN):
   - The pain is now the headline: PAANCH FUNCTION. DO KAAN. ('five functions, two ears'). The relief moves to the string tag: NA BHAARI · NA BHAAV.
   - The pair rests on a teased tuft of white cotton wool inside the paper packet. That is how jewellers wrap small pieces, and what every sore lobe has known: the picture now says weightless, and the white kills the oxblood cast on the clear stones.
   - The field of view drops to 5.5 cm, so 'Shown magnified' is honest at about 20 px/mm.
   - The ticker now reads PAANCH FUNCTION · EK JODI · ₹1,049.
10. Card 10 (OFFER): the beat is in her voice: 'do dene ke, ek rakhne ka.' The slip's lines are now Hinglish ('didi ke liye', 'apne liye'), and a corner of indigo carbon paper peeks from the pad.
11. Scale honesty: 'SHOWN MAGNIFIED' is printed only on cards 1, 3 and 9, where the 19 px/mm rule is met; cards 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 10 print their listed size plainly.
12. Copy lint (run on every headline, beat, card line and primary text): there are no digits or ₹ in Velista; no banned words; no bare gold or silver; no claims on Toggle, Verdant Cushion, Bougainvillea or Torsade. Every primary text is 147-164 characters, with BUY3 inside the first 125.

OWNER CHECKS BEFORE LAUNCH
1. Free shipping. This step's standing rules say never print free shipping, but the owner's ruling of 20 Nov (concept-50 RULINGS §6) asks for 'FREE INSURED SHIPPING · CASH ON DELIVERY' on every ad, so the footer follows the owner. On 20 Nov the shipping profile still charged ₹150 below ₹3,000. Either the checkout matches the ads before launch, or 'FREE INSURED SHIPPING' comes off the footer.
2. 'Kal bhi yahi' is a price promise. Run it only if all ten prices hold for the whole flight.
3. The slip's line 'MAKING CHARGE NAHI · WASTAGE NAHI' is true (no such charge is ever added), but it is a deliberate jab at the jewellery-bill habit and needs the owner's yes.
4. BUY4 (30%) is printed on card 2 and in the carousel text only after the margin check; otherwise those lines read 'BUY 3 · 20% OFF ANY THREE'.

   - Serpentine gold sits at the floor of 20 (named swap: Halo Curve Ring, 4 g listed, ₹899, 27 in stock).

ads.motion:
Kling 3.0, 5 s, made from the chosen still.
- 0-0.6 s: near black.
- 0.6-1.1 s: the tube-light streak in the glass stutters on twice (two ticks) and holds.
- 1.1-5 s: the amber haze at the top edge breathes slowly, as if the sign above has just lit. The camera pushes in 3%, with no orbit. The velvet nap catches the light.
- The hoops stay perfectly rigid throughout: no rotation, no sparkle, no reflections sliding on the satin.

HTML in post:
- 0-0.6 s: the SVG rolling shutter covers the frame, then rattles up into its drum at the top edge, with a 6 px bounce. The fascia lights as the drum fades.
- 0.8-1.8 s: the board flickers on row by row. The marquee 'AAJ KA BHAAV · KAL KA BHAAV · PARSON KA BHAAV' scrolls through, then settles into the AAJ and KAL rows.
- 1.8-3.0 s: both price fields roll upward as blurred digit strips, like a live rate update. Nothing legible holds for more than one frame.
- 3.0 s: both rows clunk back onto exactly ₹699 /JODI, with an LED beep.
- 3.4-4.6 s: the gold-light THOK BHAAV row scrolls in.
- 4.4 s: the H1 and the counter strip fade up.

Sound: shutter rattle, tube-light hum, two ticks, one beep.
ads.risk: Brushed satin polished into a mirror, or turned orange by the amber haze. In one second the joke resolves her loudest money worry, and the camp opens on the lowest price on the list, so the first click is the easiest yes.

camps.name: PAINTED BIGGEST.
camps.idea:
WORLD: every ad is a folio from a royal album. The real piece, with its real shadow, lies on a commissioned gouache miniature on wasli paper. In the painting, palaces, gardens, elephants and whole cities are fingernail-sized, so the jewel is the biggest thing in the picture. That is hieratic scale, the old painters' rule: the most important thing is drawn biggest. The piece is never enlarged. The world is painted small, the album frame is a ruler, and every ad states the real size.

THE PUSH, A SECOND RULE: EVERYTHING FACES THE JEWEL. Each painting behaves as if the piece were its sun or its king:
- cranes fly toward it;
- elephants walk toward it or queue at it;
- lamp-lit windows face it;
- on card 1, every painted shadow is cast by the stones.
Size makes the piece the biggest thing in the picture. Behaviour makes it the most important.

TEN PAGES, TEN SCHOOLS:
1. Halo Curve: a Mewar hill palace under a sky split into noon and midnight.
2. Toggle: a Marwar desert road, where a riderless baraat walks up the chain to the clasp.
3. Verdant Circlet: a Kishangarh night lake, the only water in the campaign.
4. Molten Panel: a Mughal charbagh walled in by the bangle, with nine elephants locked out.
5. Bold Dome: a golden city of domes, whose overlay builds a palace from three pieces.
6. Woven: a Jaipur facade of four hundred and twelve windows, one of them lit.
7. Triple Coil: a Jaipur bangle bazaar under a giant real wrist.
8. Quatrefoil: a Bikaner desert night whose stars fall onto the dune.
9. Petite Square: a chaupar courtyard.
10. Torsade: a Bundi garden of facing pavilions.

THE ARCHITECTURE TRILOGY: cards 2, 4 and 5 are a gate, a wall and a dome. So card 5's BUY3 is not a discount poster but a palace: DOME, GATE, WALL, worn at the ear, neck and wrist.

RULES:
- No human or deity figures in any painting.
- Animals appear only as tiny profile silhouettes.
- No inscriptions in the paintings: all type is HTML.
- No copy of any museum miniature.
- Painted water appears only on card 3 (the Verdant Circlet is tagged waterproof). Every other page is dry.
- One product per picture. Card 5's spread is a composite of three separately generated pictures.

THE GRAFT: Naira commissions a living Rajasthani miniature painter, pays for advertising rights and credits the painter on every ad. The AI version of each page is only the layout comp and the painter's brief, and it is never published. The best version photographs the real piece on the real page with the two-light set-up (the prompt doubles as the shot list). The fallback is the Higgsfield frame, with the painting as reference 3.

MOTION, FOUR REELS (the piece never moves):
- Card 2 (Kling): a riderless baraat walks up the chain while kettle-drums beat by themselves, and the last firework bursts in the shape of the clasp.
- Card 3 (HTML only, no credits): a slip of tracing paper folds over the axis, and the traced stud lands on its twin. Q.E.D.
- Card 6 (HTML only): a gold marker draws the group-photo circle round the one lit window.
- Card 8 (Kling): two painted shooting stars fall from the sky and land exactly where the studs lie.

RUN ORDER: cards 1-5 first (Halo, Toggle, Circlet, Molten, then Dome with the palace spread). Then cards 6-10 (Woven, Coil, Quatrefoil, Square, then Torsade with the treasury register).
camps.insight:
She is never the biggest thing in her own wedding photos. There are three hundred guests, a stage and a mandap, and her earrings come out as four pixels.

Indian painters solved this four hundred years ago. They drew the most important thing biggest, and they turned the whole world toward it. Put a real piece on a painted world and it honestly becomes the biggest thing in the picture, without one false millimetre. Make the painted world face it, and it becomes the most important thing too.

This is Think Small turned inside out. Volkswagen made the car small on an empty page; Naira makes the world small round a ₹899 piece.

Miniatures are the art of India's grand homes right now, so a piece laid on one borrows heirloom value. A credited living painter makes it culture rather than pastiche.

For slow stock this matters most. These pieces have not been seen. A folio gives each one a reason to be looked at now, in wedding season, and a series of ten gives her a reason to collect three.
camps.textualGraphic:
THE FOLIO is a type and graphic system built for hieratic scale. It is made in HTML/SVG over the plate, with kit.css tokens and fonts.

(1) THE ALBUM FRAME
- The outer edge is a 26 px band of abri marbled paper in SVG. Filter: feTurbulence type 'turbulence', baseFrequency '0.004 0.05', 3 octaves, then feDisplacementMap scale 70, over stripes of the folio's two colours.
- Veins: 1 px gold-light #E4C889 hairlines.
- Zar-afshan flecks: 120 irregular gold-light polygons, 1-4 px, 40-80% opacity, on the band only.
- Inside the band is the jadval, the album's ruled border: 8 px oxblood, 3 px gap, 2 px gold-light, 3 px gap, 1 px bone, with a 34 px gold-light lotus-bud fleuron at each corner.
- The bottom band is 54 px (Feed) or 64 px (Story) and carries the footer.
- The painting fills the frame inside the jadval: the frame is the album, and the plate is the page.

(2) THE JADVAL RULER (new)
- The innermost 1 px bone rule of the jadval is a true-scale ruler, ticked at the plate's measured px per mm:
  - 1 mm ticks: 4 px;
  - 5 mm ticks: 8 px;
  - 10 mm ticks: 12 px, numbered in Jost 400 22 px bone at 70% (top and left edges only).
- The frame itself is the measuring instrument, so the real size is the border of every page, not a claim tucked in a corner.
- It is computed per plate from the same px per mm as the scale bar, so it can never disagree with it.

(3) THE INSCRIPTION CARTOUCHE
- Old paintings carried their inscription in a panel at the top; ours carries the headline.
- Shape: an SVG lobed cartouche, a long panel whose short ends close in ogee points.
  - Feed: 860 x 206 at x 110, y 84.
  - Story: 900 x 236 at x 90, y 270.
- Fill: cocoa #3B2620 (night) or oxblood (day) at 94%, with a 2 px gold-light inner rule inset 10 px and a 16 px six-petal gold-light rosette at each point.
- Headline: Velista caps in bone #F4F0E8, 70-92 px Feed (88-116 Story), tracking .04em, ligatures off, balanced to two lines at most.
- Beat: Cormorant Garamond italic 500, 38-44 px, gold-light.

(4) THE HIERATIC CAPTION
- Every ad carries it; it is the line that owns the scale.
- A bone strip (90%, 2 px oxblood hairline, padding 12/18) sits just under the piece. It holds:
  - the fixed kicker in Cormorant italic 500 30 px ink: 'Old painters drew the most important thing biggest.';
  - under it, the honest size in Jost 500 caps 26 px .14em oxblood, for example 'REAL SIZE: 17 MM INSIDE'.
- Above the strip, a hairline scale bar is drawn at the plate's px per mm along the dimension named: 1.5 px gold-light, 1 mm ticks 6 px, 5 mm ticks 12 px. Its ends touch the metal at 10 px open circles.
- At or above 19 Feed px per listed mm, the line adds '· SHOWN ENLARGED'. The prompts size every piece to its painting so that no card should need it.

(5) HIERATIC LABELS
The labels obey the painters' rule.
- Real-piece callouts are big:
  - a 40 px gold-light roundel with a Jost 500 22 px ink numeral;
  - a 1.5 px leader with one elbow that ends on metal, never on a stone or pearl;
  - the label in Jost 500 caps 24-26 px .12em, plus a Cormorant italic 30 px line.
- Painted things get small labels: Jost 400 caps 22 px .16em at 75%, no roundel. The label states the painted size and, where it applies, the thing's behaviour, for example 'SHADOWS, PAINTED · CAST BY THE TIGER EYE' or 'ELEPHANT, PAINTED · 3 MM · STILL OUTSIDE'.
- At most three real labels and one painted label per ad.
- Every painted size or count is measured (or counted) on the plate that ships, at that plate's px per mm, before print. If it differs, the label prints the measured figure or drops the number.

(6) THE F2 CARTOUCHE
- The lobed shape, mirrored.
  - Feed: 900 x 330 at y 905.
  - Story: 920 x 250 at y 1000.
- It holds the F2 lockup:
  - Naira wordmark (logo_white), 48 px;
  - NAME in Jost 500 caps 26 px .2em;
  - price in Cormorant 500 56 px (₹ from Noto Serif);
  - one line in Jost 26 px;
  - offer box in Jost 500 caps 26 px .14em, with a 2 px gold-light hairline and the kit's rotated-square separator. On SELL cards the box fills saffron with ink type.

(7) THE COLLECTOR'S SEAL
- Album pages carry the round seals of the libraries that owned them; ours is Naira's.
- A 118 px oxblood roundel (3 px ring, 1 px inner ring, the wordmark across the centre) with an feTurbulence stamp-ink mask, rotated -9 degrees and overlapping the lower-left jadval.
- On card 5 it stamps across the gutter. On card 10 it stamps the treasury register.

(8) THE PAINTER'S CREDIT
Jost 400 22 px bone at 80%, along the bottom jadval: 'Painted for Naira by [painter], [town] · gouache on wasli · the jewellery is real'. The clause '· the jewellery is real' prints only on a folio where the real piece was photographed on the real page; on a Higgsfield fallback frame the credit ends at 'gouache on wasli'.

(9) THE FOLIO MARK (new)
- A cocoa spine tab on the right jadval, set vertically and reading upward: 'FOLIO IV · OF X' in Jost 500 caps 22 px .2em gold-light.
- Feed y 320-560; Story y 520-760.
- The ten ads read as one album. A viewer who has seen two knows there are ten, which turns retargeting into collecting.

(10) CARD DEVICES grow out of each painting:
- Card 1: the headline, beat, F2 cartouche and price all switch colour at the noon/midnight seam.
- Card 2: a cartouche that unrolls, a procession that walks, and a firework drawn as the clasp.
- Card 3: the tracing-paper fold, traced above and landing below, Q.E.D.
- Card 4: a dictionary footnote (†) and a second note (‡ the elephants are still outside).
- Card 5: an architect's elevation key: A THE DOME, B THE GATE, C THE WALL, worn at ear, neck and wrist.
- Card 6: a hand-drawn gold marker circle round the one lit window: 'THAT'S YOU.'
- Card 7: twelve hairline bangles in twelve colours, struck through.
- Card 8: a translation gloss under the Hinglish.
- Card 9: the four pearls counted 1 to 4 in the four Ludo colours.
- Card 10: a royal treasury register with three measured entries and an empty fourth line.

GRID
- Plates are 9:16 at 4K. The piece sits in the band from 26% to 53% of the height, with calm painted sky from 13% to 25% and calm painted ground below 54%.
- Story uses the full plate: headline cartouche from y 270, piece y 500-1000, F2 y 1000-1250, footer y 1262.
- Feed crops the plate from 10% to 80%: cartouche y 84-290, piece y 310-830, caption y 820-880, F2 y 905-1235.
- Text stays under about 30% of the frame. The smallest type is 22 px.
camps.brandFeatures:
The Naira wordmark appears twice, the way a page from a royal album carries it:
- in the F2 cartouche (logo_white 48 px);
- as the collector's seal, an oxblood ink roundel stamped on the lower-left corner of every folio: the mark of whoever owns the album.

The F2 card keeps its full grammar inside the lower cartouche (wordmark, name, price, one line, offer box), so every ad still ends as Naira.

The new folio mark ('FOLIO I · OF X' to 'FOLIO X · OF X') makes the ten ads one owned series, and the jadval ruler makes 'real size' a Naira signature. No other Indian jewellery brand frames its pieces in a ruler.

Type stays in the kit's three families:
- Velista for the inscription;
- Cormorant italic for the beat, the kicker, the footnotes and the prices;
- Jost for real sizes, labels, the ruler, the credit and the footer.

Colours come from the palette tokens only.

Every ad carries the footer 'INSURED SHIPPING · CASH ON DELIVERY'. 'FREE' goes in front of it (owner ruling §6, 20 Nov) only once the pre-flight read shows the checkout charging ₹0 shipping at every basket size; on 20 Nov it still charged ₹150 below ₹3,000 (see changes).

The painter's credit line is part of the brand: Naira commissions artists.

Each ad is delivered as Feed 4:5 and Story 9:16 from one 9:16 plate. Cards 2, 3, 6 and 8 also come as 5-second Reels.

camps.sellLever:
Hieratic scale turns the purchase into self-worth: you are the most important thing in the picture, so wear the biggest thing in it in this season's wedding photos. The camp then makes three pieces the natural unit, twice and in two different ways.

CARD 5, THE PALACE
- DOME, GATE, WALL: every palace needs three things, and so does the look. Ear, neck and wrist each come from a card she has already seen (the Toggle's gate on card 2, the Molten Panel's wall on card 4, the Bold Dome here).
- The basket is Bold Dome ₹999 + Toggle ₹999 + Molten Panel ₹999 = ₹2,997, which is about ₹2,398 after BUY3.

CARD 10, THE TREASURY REGISTER
- Three measured entries are already written in: Torsade ₹1,099, Quatrefoil ₹1,099, Toggle ₹999. That is ₹3,197, about ₹2,558 after BUY3.
- An empty fourth line invites BUY4. Adding the Woven (₹1,049) gives ₹4,246, about ₹2,972 at 30% off.

EVERY OTHER AD
- Every primary text carries 'Any three, 20% off with BUY3' before character 125.
- Every F2 carries the BUY2/BUY3 box.
- The folio mark tells her there are ten to choose from.

THE TWO ANCHORS
- The Toggle (77 in stock, ₹999) appears in both baskets.
- The Woven (88 in stock) gets a PAIN card of its own with a SELL box.

THE MATHS FOR ROAS 5
At a basket of about ₹2,400, ROAS 5 needs one purchase per ₹480 of spend: about 10 purchases a day at ₹5,000 a day. That is the lever. Today's order value is roughly half of this basket, and today's ROAS is 2.2.
camps.carouselText: Old painters drew the most important thing biggest, and painted the whole world turning toward it. So we laid real jewellery on hand-painted miniatures where whole palaces are fingernail-sized. Build the palace: a dome, a gate and a wall. Any three, 20% off with BUY3; any four, 30% off with BUY4. Real sizes on every folio.

- windows are lit toward it;

It is a system rule a jury can find on every page.

ads.title: Sun and moon
ads.variant: Default Title, 18k gold tone (the only variant). Stock 27.
ads.picture:
WHAT IT SHOWS: a Mewar hill palace under a sky split down the middle by one clean vertical seam, saffron noon on the left and indigo midnight on the right.

THE STONES ARE THE SUN AND MOON: no sun and no moon are painted, because the ring brings them. The opaque banded tiger eye sits on the day side, the pale champagne crystal on the night side, and the seam runs exactly between their nearly touching corners.

THE PAINTED WORLD OBEYS THEM:
- On the day side, every painted turret and cypress throws a thin painted shadow pointing straight away from the tiger eye, as if the stone were the sun, and three tiny cranes fly toward it.
- On the night side, the palace's tiny windows glow only on the side that faces the crystal.

THE GROUND: the palace stands on a honey-ochre rock spur, with plain dry ground below. There is no lake, so card 3 owns the water.

SCALE: the ring is wider than the palace, and its real shadow falls across the painted sky.

REFERENCES:
- Ref 1: listing 02 (cube, construction), media ac8bad23-c21e-447f-801c-3ec328d118f6.
- Ref 2: listing 01 (worn, scale), media d99052b5-4023-4077-8006-2e78f1f875d1.
- Ref 3: the commissioned page, when it arrives.

PAINTER'S BRIEF: 15 x 27 cm; the seam a ruled line; palace 20 mm; all painted shadows drawn from one vanishing point at a pinprick where the tiger eye will lie; sky above the palace left plain.

WHY IT STOPS THE THUMB: half the picture is noon and half is midnight, the only two lights in it are the stones, and the painting's own shadows prove it.

Each end holds 1 cushion stone in 1 slim plain bezel, set diagonally, corners nearly touching: 1 opaque banded golden-brown tiger eye about 11.8mm with a softly faceted top, and 1 transparent faceted pale champagne crystal of about the same face. 0 pave, 0 prongs, high polish. ads.primaryText: He promised to bring down the stars. Here are two, ₹1,099. Any three, 20% off with BUY3. Four pear-cut stones in a pavé outline, 15 mm, 18k gold tone. Pre-order.
ads.motion:
Kling 3.0, 5 s, 9:16, from the approved still. The studs never move.

THE WORLD:
- 0-1.2 s: one painted shooting star streaks down from the upper right and ends exactly at the left stud's position.
- 1.4-2.6 s: a second one falls and ends exactly at the right stud.
- The streak paths are drawn in After Effects as flat painted strokes with a gouache texture, so they land on the measured stud centres. As each streak ends, a composited glint flares across that stud's four pear-cut stones and runs round its pavé outline once. The promise is shown being kept.
- 0-5 s: the hundreds of painted four-point stars twinkle a few at a time (each swells and fades over half a second, like hand-painted frames), and the riderless camel caravan walks slowly along the dune crest toward the studs, about 1.5 cm in 5 s, with a flat paper-cut sway.

LIGHT: after the landings, a soft composited kicker sweep of 10 degrees moves glints across the stones. The metal and stones keep their shape.

CAMERA: locked, then a 2% drift upward toward the sky in the last 1.5 s.

PROTECTION: the studs and their shadows are a hard matte from the still. All glints are composited highlights masked to the stones, so Kling never redraws the construction. Kling animates only the twinkling and the caravan.
- Kling prompt tail: 'a moving miniature painting, flat painted stars twinkle and flat painted camels sway forward, the gold-tone studs are real, rigid and perfectly still, no people, no faces, no new objects, no text'.

SOUND FOR REELS: a soft santoor shimmer on each landing and on the twinkles. Also export a silent version.
ads.risk:
MAIN RISK, THE OUTLINE: the product name pulls the model toward a rounded four-leaf clover or a solid pavé face, and the pears may multiply into a six- or eight-point snowflake.

SECOND RISK: the painted stars rendered as real glitter or real crystals on the paper.

HEDGE TAKE: the same plate with the studs on the indigo sky and the painted stars kept as round dots, so nothing on the paper shares the studs' shape. The shooting stars then land 'in' the sky.
ads.why10: 'Chaand taare tod laana' is the oldest lovers' promise in Hindi, and here it is kept. Two four-point stars lie on the dunes under a sky painted with hundreds of tiny ones in the same shape, and in the Reel two stars fall and land exactly where the studs lie. It sells the outcome, feeling cherished, both to her and to the young men 18-24 who buy gifts ('He promised…'). It also teaches the construction (four pear-cut stones in a pavé outline, 15 mm) by naming the stars.
